1: //! Rewriting strategies for circuit optimisation.
2: //!
3: //! This module contains the [`RewriteStrategy`] trait, which is currently
4: //! implemented by
5: //! - [`GreedyRewriteStrategy`], which applies as many rewrites as possible on
6: //!   one circuit, and
7: //! - Exhaustive strategies, which clone the original circuit and explore every
8: //!   possible rewrite (with some pruning strategy):
9: //!    - [`ExhaustiveGreedyStrategy`], which applies multiple combinations of
10: //!      non-overlapping rewrites.
11: //!    - [`ExhaustiveThresholdStrategy`], which tries every rewrite below
12: //!      threshold function.
13: //!
14: //! The exhaustive strategies are parametrised by a strategy cost function:
15: //!    - [`LexicographicCostFunction`] allows rewrites that do
16: //!      not increase some coarse cost function (e.g. CX count), whilst
17: //!      ordering them according to a lexicographic ordering of finer cost
18: //!      functions (e.g. total gate count). See
19: //!      [`LexicographicCostFunction::default_cx`]) for a default implementation.
20: //!    - [`GammaStrategyCost`] ignores rewrites that increase the cost
21: //!      function beyond a percentage given by a f64 parameter gamma.
22: 
23: use std::{collections::HashSet, fmt::Debug};
24: 
25: use derive_more::From;
26: use hugr::ops::OpType;
27: use hugr::Hugr;
28: use itertools::Itertools;
29: 
30: use crate::circuit::cost::{is_cx, is_quantum, CircuitCost, CostDelta, LexicographicCost};
31: use crate::Circuit;
32: 
33: use super::trace::{RewriteTrace, RewriteTracer};
34: use super::CircuitRewrite;
35: 
36: /// Rewriting strategies for circuit optimisation.
37: ///
38: /// A rewrite strategy takes a set of possible rewrites and applies them
39: /// to a circuit according to a strategy. It returns a list of new circuits,
40: /// each obtained by applying one or several non-overlapping rewrites to the
41: /// original circuit.
42: ///
43: /// It also assign every circuit a totally ordered cost that can be used when
44: /// using rewrites for circuit optimisation.
45: pub trait RewriteStrategy {
46:     /// The circuit cost to be minimised.
47:     type Cost: CircuitCost;
48: 
49:     /// Apply a set of rewrites to a circuit.
50:     fn apply_rewrites(
51:         &self,
52:         rewrites: impl IntoIterator<Item = CircuitRewrite>,
53:         circ: &Hugr,
54:     ) -> RewriteResult<Self::Cost>;
55: 
56:     /// The cost of a single operation for this strategy's cost function.
57:     fn op_cost(&self, op: &OpType) -> Self::Cost;
58: 
59:     /// The cost of a circuit using this strategy's cost function.
60:     #[inline]
61:     fn circuit_cost(&self, circ: &Hugr) -> Self::Cost {
62:         circ.circuit_cost(|op| self.op_cost(op))
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Returns the cost of a rewrite's matched subcircuit before replacing it.
66:     #[inline]
67:     fn pre_rewrite_cost(&self, rw: &CircuitRewrite, circ: &Hugr) -> Self::Cost {
68:         circ.nodes_cost(rw.subcircuit().nodes().iter().copied(), |op| {
69:             self.op_cost(op)
70:         })
71:     }
72: 
73:     /// Returns the expected cost of a rewrite's matched subcircuit after replacing it.
74:     fn post_rewrite_cost(&self, rw: &CircuitRewrite) -> Self::Cost {
75:         rw.replacement().circuit_cost(|op| self.op_cost(op))
76:     }
77: }
78: 
79: /// The result of a rewrite strategy.
80: ///
81: /// Returned by [`RewriteStrategy::apply_rewrites`].
82: pub struct RewriteResult<Cost: CircuitCost> {
83:     /// The rewritten circuits.
84:     pub circs: Vec<Hugr>,
85:     /// The cost delta of each rewritten circuit.
86:     pub cost_deltas: Vec<Cost::CostDelta>,
87: }
88: 
89: impl<Cost: CircuitCost> RewriteResult<Cost> {
90:     /// Init a new rewrite result.
91:     pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {
92:         Self {
93:             circs: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),
94:             cost_deltas: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     /// Returns the number of rewritten circuits.
99:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
100:         self.circs.len()
101:     }
102: 
103:     /// Returns true if there are no rewritten circuits.
104:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
105:         self.circs.is_empty()
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Returns an iterator over the rewritten circuits and their cost deltas.
109:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&Hugr, &Cost::CostDelta)> {
110:         self.circs.iter().zip(self.cost_deltas.iter())
111:     }
112: }
113: 
114: impl<Cost: CircuitCost> IntoIterator for RewriteResult<Cost> {
115:     type Item = (Hugr, Cost::CostDelta);
116:     type IntoIter = std::iter::Zip<std::vec::IntoIter<Hugr>, std::vec::IntoIter<Cost::CostDelta>>;
117: 
118:     fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
119:         self.circs.into_iter().zip(self.cost_deltas)
120:     }
121: }
122: 
123: /// A rewrite strategy applying as many non-overlapping rewrites as possible.
124: ///
125: /// All possible rewrites are sorted by the number of gates they remove from
126: /// the circuit and are applied in order. If a rewrite overlaps with a rewrite
127: /// that has already been applied, it is skipped.
128: ///
129: /// This strategy will always return exactly one circuit: the original circuit
130: /// with as many rewrites applied as possible.
131: ///
132: /// Rewrites are only applied if they strictly decrease gate count.
133: #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
134: pub struct GreedyRewriteStrategy;
135: 
136: impl RewriteStrategy for GreedyRewriteStrategy {
137:     type Cost = usize;
138: 
139:     #[tracing::instrument(skip_all)]
140:     fn apply_rewrites(
141:         &self,
142:         rewrites: impl IntoIterator<Item = CircuitRewrite>,
143:         circ: &Hugr,
144:     ) -> RewriteResult<usize> {
145:         let rewrites = rewrites
146:             .into_iter()
147:             .sorted_by_key(|rw| rw.node_count_delta())
148:             .take_while(|rw| rw.node_count_delta() < 0);
149:         let mut changed_nodes = HashSet::new();
150:         let mut cost_delta = 0;
151:         let mut circ = circ.clone();
152:         for rewrite in rewrites {
153:             if rewrite
154:                 .subcircuit()
155:                 .nodes()
156:                 .iter()
157:                 .any(|n| changed_nodes.contains(n))
158:             {
159:                 continue;
160:             }
161:             changed_nodes.extend(rewrite.subcircuit().nodes().iter().copied());
162:             cost_delta += rewrite.node_count_delta();
163:             rewrite
164:                 .apply(&mut circ)
165:                 .expect("Could not perform rewrite in greedy strategy");
166:         }
167:         RewriteResult {
168:             circs: vec![circ],
169:             cost_deltas: vec![cost_delta],
170:         }
171:     }
172: 
173:     fn circuit_cost(&self, circ: &Hugr) -> Self::Cost {
174:         circ.num_gates()
175:     }
176: 
177:     fn op_cost(&self, _op: &OpType) -> Self::Cost {
178:         1
179:     }
180: }
181: 
182: /// Exhaustive strategies based on cost functions and thresholds.
183: ///
184: /// Every possible rewrite is applied to a copy of the input circuit. In
185: /// addition, other non-overlapping rewrites are applied greedily in ascending
186: /// cost delta.
187: ///
188: /// Thus for one circuit, up to `n` rewritten circuits will be returned, each
189: /// obtained by applying at least one of the `n` rewrites to the original
190: /// circuit.
191: ///
192: /// Whether a rewrite is allowed or not is determined by a cost function and a
193: /// threshold function: if the cost of the target of the rewrite is below the
194: /// threshold given by the cost of the original circuit, the rewrite is
195: /// performed.
196: ///
197: /// The cost function must return a value of type `Self::OpCost`. All op costs
198: /// are summed up to obtain a total cost that is then compared using the
199: /// threshold function.
200: ///
201: /// This kind of strategy is not recommended for thresholds that allow positive
202: /// cost deltas, as these will always be greedily applied even if they increase
203: /// the final cost.
204: #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, From)]
205: pub struct ExhaustiveGreedyStrategy<T> {
206:     /// The cost function.
207:     pub strat_cost: T,
208: }
209: 
210: impl<T: StrategyCost> RewriteStrategy for ExhaustiveGreedyStrategy<T> {
211:     type Cost = T::OpCost;
212: 
213:     #[tracing::instrument(skip_all)]
214:     fn apply_rewrites(
215:         &self,
216:         rewrites: impl IntoIterator<Item = CircuitRewrite>,
217:         circ: &Hugr,
218:     ) -> RewriteResult<T::OpCost> {
219:         // Check only the rewrites that reduce the size of the circuit.
220:         let rewrites = rewrites
221:             .into_iter()
222:             .filter_map(|rw| {
223:                 let pattern_cost = self.pre_rewrite_cost(&rw, circ);
224:                 let target_cost = self.post_rewrite_cost(&rw);
225:                 if !self.strat_cost.under_threshold(&pattern_cost, &target_cost) {
226:                     return None;
227:                 }
228:                 Some((rw, target_cost.sub_cost(&pattern_cost)))
229:             })
230:             .sorted_by_key(|(_, delta)| delta.clone())
231:             .collect_vec();
232: 
233:         let mut rewrite_sets = RewriteResult::with_capacity(rewrites.len());
234:         for i in 0..rewrites.len() {
235:             let mut curr_circ = circ.clone();
236:             let mut changed_nodes = HashSet::new();
237:             let mut cost_delta = Default::default();
238:             let mut composed_rewrite_count = 0;
239:             for (rewrite, delta) in &rewrites[i..] {
240:                 if !changed_nodes.is_empty()
241:                     && rewrite
242:                         .invalidation_set()
243:                         .any(|n| changed_nodes.contains(&n))
244:                 {
245:                     continue;
246:                 }
247:                 changed_nodes.extend(rewrite.invalidation_set());
248:                 cost_delta += delta.clone();
249: 
250:                 composed_rewrite_count += 1;
251: 
252:                 rewrite
253:                     .clone()
254:                     .apply_notrace(&mut curr_circ)
255:                     .expect("Could not perform rewrite in exhaustive greedy strategy");
256:             }
257: 
258:             curr_circ.add_rewrite_trace(RewriteTrace::new(composed_rewrite_count));
259:             rewrite_sets.circs.push(curr_circ);
260:             rewrite_sets.cost_deltas.push(cost_delta);
261:         }
262:         rewrite_sets
263:     }
264: 
265:     #[inline]
266:     fn op_cost(&self, op: &OpType) -> Self::Cost {
267:         self.strat_cost.op_cost(op)
268:     }
269: }
270: 
271: /// Exhaustive strategies based on cost functions and thresholds.
272: ///
273: /// Every possible rewrite is applied to a copy of the input circuit. Thus for
274: /// one circuit, up to `n` rewritten circuits will be returned, each obtained
275: /// by applying one of the `n` rewrites to the original circuit.
276: ///
277: /// Whether a rewrite is allowed or not is determined by a cost function and a
278: /// threshold function: if the cost of the target of the rewrite is below the
279: /// threshold given by the cost of the original circuit, the rewrite is
280: /// performed.
281: ///
282: /// The cost function must return a value of type `Self::OpCost`. All op costs
283: /// are summed up to obtain a total cost that is then compared using the
284: /// threshold function.
285: #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, From)]
286: pub struct ExhaustiveThresholdStrategy<T> {
287:     /// The cost function.
288:     pub strat_cost: T,
289: }
290: 
291: impl<T: StrategyCost> RewriteStrategy for ExhaustiveThresholdStrategy<T> {
292:     type Cost = T::OpCost;
293: 
294:     #[tracing::instrument(skip_all)]
295:     fn apply_rewrites(
296:         &self,
297:         rewrites: impl IntoIterator<Item = CircuitRewrite>,
298:         circ: &Hugr,
299:     ) -> RewriteResult<T::OpCost> {
300:         let (circs, cost_deltas) = rewrites
301:             .into_iter()
302:             .filter_map(|rw| {
303:                 let pattern_cost = self.pre_rewrite_cost(&rw, circ);
304:                 let target_cost = self.post_rewrite_cost(&rw);
305:                 if !self.strat_cost.under_threshold(&pattern_cost, &target_cost) {
306:                     return None;
307:                 }
308:                 let mut circ = circ.clone();
309:                 rw.apply(&mut circ).expect("invalid pattern match");
310:                 Some((circ, target_cost.sub_cost(&pattern_cost)))
311:             })
312:             .unzip();
313:         RewriteResult { circs, cost_deltas }
314:     }
315: 
316:     #[inline]
317:     fn op_cost(&self, op: &OpType) -> Self::Cost {
318:         self.strat_cost.op_cost(op)
319:     }
320: }
321: 
322: /// Cost function definitions required in exhaustive strategies.
323: ///
324: /// See [`ExhaustiveThresholdStrategy`], [`ExhaustiveGreedyStrategy`].
325: pub trait StrategyCost {
326:     /// The cost of a single operation.
327:     type OpCost: CircuitCost;
328: 
329:     /// Returns true if the rewrite is allowed, based on the cost of the pattern and target.
330:     #[inline]
331:     fn under_threshold(&self, pattern_cost: &Self::OpCost, target_cost: &Self::OpCost) -> bool {
332:         target_cost.sub_cost(pattern_cost).as_isize() <= 0
333:     }
334: 
335:     /// The cost of a single operation.
336:     fn op_cost(&self, op: &OpType) -> Self::OpCost;
337: }
338: 
339: /// Rewrite strategy cost allowing smaller or equal cost rewrites.
340: ///
341: /// Rewrites are permitted based on a coarse cost function: if
342: /// the coarse cost of the target of the rewrite is smaller or equal to the
343: /// coarse cost of the pattern, the rewrite is allowed.
344: ///
345: /// Further more fine-grained cost functions can be used as tie breakers: within
346: /// circuits with the same coarse cost, circuits are ranked according to a
347: /// lexicographic ordering of their cost functions.
348: ///
349: /// An example would be to use the number of CX gates as coarse cost and the
350: /// total number of gates as the only fine grained cost function.
351: ///
352: /// Lexicographic orderings may be useful to add relief to an otherwise flat
353: /// optimisation landscape.

356:     cost_fns: [F; N],
357: }

364:

367:         let mut costs = [0; N];
368:         for (cost_fn, cost_mut) in self.cost_fns.iter().zip(&mut costs) {
369:             *cost_mut = cost_fn(op);
370:         }
371:         costs.into()

391: /// Rewrite strategy cost allowing rewrites with bounded cost increase.
392: ///
393: /// The parameter gamma controls how greedy the algorithm should be. It allows a
394: /// rewrite C1 -> C2 if C2 has at most gamma times the cost of C1:
395: ///
396: /// $cost(C2) < gamma * cost(C1)$
397: ///
398: /// The cost function is given by the sum of the cost of each operation in the
399: /// circuit. This allows for instance to use of the total number of gates (true
400: /// predicate), the number of CX gates or a weighted sum of gate types as cost
401: /// functions.

403: /// gamma = 1 is the greedy strategy where a rewrite is only allowed if it
404: /// strictly reduces the gate count. The default is gamma = 1.0001 (as set in

159: /// Remove an empty wire in a dataflow HUGR.
160: ///
161: /// The wire to be removed is identified by the index of the outgoing port
162: /// at the circuit input node.
163: ///
164: /// This will change the circuit signature and will shift all ports after
165: /// the removed wire by -1. If the wire is connected to the output node,
166: /// this will also change the signature output and shift the ports after
167: /// the removed wire by -1.
168: ///
169: /// This will return an error if the wire is not empty or if a HugrError
170: /// occurs.
171: #[allow(dead_code)]
172: pub(crate) fn remove_empty_wire(
173:     circ: &mut impl HugrMut,
174:     input_port: usize,
175: ) -> Result<(), CircuitMutError> {
176:     let [inp, out] = circ.get_io(circ.root()).expect("no IO nodes found at root");
177:     if input_port >= circ.num_outputs(inp) {
178:         return Err(CircuitMutError::InvalidPortOffset(input_port));
179:     }
180:     let input_port = Port::new(Direction::Outgoing, input_port);
181:     let link = circ
182:         .linked_ports(inp, input_port)
183:         .at_most_one()
184:         .map_err(|_| CircuitMutError::DeleteNonEmptyWire(input_port.index()))?;
185:     if link.is_some() && link.unwrap().0 != out {
186:         return Err(CircuitMutError::DeleteNonEmptyWire(input_port.index()));
187:     }
188:     if link.is_some() {
189:         circ.disconnect(inp, input_port)?;
190:     }
191: 
192:     // Shift ports at input
193:     shift_ports(circ, inp, input_port, circ.num_outputs(inp))?;
194:     // Shift ports at output
195:     if let Some((out, output_port)) = link {
196:         shift_ports(circ, out, output_port, circ.num_inputs(out))?;
197:     }
198:     // Update input node, output node (if necessary) and root signatures.
199:     update_signature(circ, input_port.index(), link.map(|(_, p)| p.index()));
200:     // Resize ports at input/output node
201:     circ.set_num_ports(inp, 0, circ.num_outputs(inp) - 1);
202:     if let Some((out, _)) = link {
203:         circ.set_num_ports(out, circ.num_inputs(out) - 1, 0);
204:     }
205:     Ok(())
206: }

224: /// Shift ports in range (free_port + 1 .. max_ind) by -1.
225: fn shift_ports<C: HugrMut + ?Sized>(
226:     circ: &mut C,
227:     node: Node,
228:     mut free_port: Port,
229:     max_ind: usize,
230: ) -> Result<Port, hugr::hugr::HugrError> {
231:     let dir = free_port.direction();
232:     let port_range = (free_port.index() + 1..max_ind).map(|p| Port::new(dir, p));
233:     for port in port_range {
234:         let links = circ.linked_ports(node, port).collect_vec();
235:         if !links.is_empty() {
236:             circ.disconnect(node, port)?;
237:         }
238:         for (other_n, other_p) in links {
239:             match other_p.as_directed() {
240:                 Right(other_p) => {
241:                     let dst_port = free_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
242:                     circ.connect(other_n, other_p, node, dst_port)
243:                 }
244:                 Left(other_p) => {
245:                     let src_port = free_port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
246:                     circ.connect(node, src_port, other_n, other_p)
247:                 }
248:             }?;
249:         }
250:         free_port = port;
251:     }
252:     Ok(free_port)
253: }

258:     circ: &mut C,
259:     in_index: usize,
260:     out_index: Option<usize>,
261: ) {
262:     let inp = circ.input();
263:     // Update input node
264:     let inp_types: TypeRow = {
265:         let OpType::Input(Input { types }) = circ.get_optype(inp).clone() else {
266:             panic!("invalid circuit")
267:         };
268:         let mut types = types.into_owned();
269:         types.remove(in_index);
270:         types.into()
271:     };
272:     let new_inp_op = Input::new(inp_types.clone());
273:     let inp_exts = circ.get_nodetype(inp).input_extensions().cloned();
274:     circ.replace_op(inp, NodeType::new(new_inp_op, inp_exts))
275:         .unwrap();
276: 
277:     // Update output node if necessary.
278:     let out_types = out_index.map(|out_index| {
279:         let out = circ.output();
280:         let out_types: TypeRow = {
281:             let OpType::Output(Output { types }) = circ.get_optype(out).clone() else {

284:             let mut types = types.into_owned();

292:         out_types

108:     /// Create a new iterator over the units of a node.
109:     //
110:     // Note that this ignores any incoming linear unit labels, and just assigns
111:     // new unit ids sequentially.
112:     #[inline]
113:     pub(super) fn new(
114:         circuit: &impl Circuit,
115:         node: Node,
116:         direction: Direction,
117:         unit_labeller: UL,
118:     ) -> Self {
119:         Self {
120:             node,
121:             direction,
122:             types: Self::init_types(circuit, node, direction),
123:             pos: 0,
124:             linear_count: 0,
125:             unit_labeller,
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Initialize the boundary types.
130:     ///
131:     /// We use a [`TypeRow`] to avoid allocating for simple boundaries, but if
132:     /// any static port is present we create a new owned [`TypeRow`] with them included.
133:     //
134:     // TODO: This is quite hacky, but we need it to accept Const static inputs.
135:     // We should revisit it once this is reworked on the HUGR side.
136:     fn init_types(circuit: &impl Circuit, node: Node, direction: Direction) -> TypeRow {
137:         let optype = circuit.get_optype(node);
138:         let sig = circuit.signature(node).unwrap_or_default();
139:         let mut types = match direction {
140:             Direction::Outgoing => sig.output,
141:             Direction::Incoming => sig.input,
142:         };
143:         if direction == Direction::Incoming {
144:             if let Some(static_port) = optype.static_input_port() {
145:                 if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(static_type)) = optype.port_kind(static_port) {
146:                     types.to_mut().push(static_type);
147:                 }
148:             }
149:         }
150:         if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(other)) = optype.other_port_kind(direction) {
151:             types.to_mut().push(other);
152:         }
153:         types
154:     }
155: 
156:     /// Construct an output value to yield.
157:     ///
158:     /// Calls [`UnitLabeller::assign_linear`] to assign a linear unit id to the linear ports.
159:     /// Non-linear ports are assigned [`CircuitUnit::Wire`]s via [`UnitLabeller::assign_wire`].
160:     #[inline]
161:     fn make_value(&self, typ: &Type, port: Port) -> Option<(CircuitUnit, Port, Type)> {
162:         let unit = if type_is_linear(typ) {
163:             let linear_unit =
164:                 self.unit_labeller
165:                     .assign_linear(self.node, port, self.linear_count - 1);
166:             CircuitUnit::Linear(linear_unit.index())
167:         } else {
168:             let wire = self.unit_labeller.assign_wire(self.node, port)?;
169:             CircuitUnit::Wire(wire)
170:         };
171:         Some((unit, port, typ.clone()))
172:     }
173: }

175: impl<UL> Iterator for Units<UL>
176: where
177:     UL: UnitLabeller,
178: {
179:     type Item = (CircuitUnit, Port, Type);
180: 
181:     #[inline]
182:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
183:         loop {
184:             let typ = self.types.get(self.pos)?;
185:             let port = Port::new(self.direction, self.pos);
186:             self.pos += 1;
187:             if type_is_linear(typ) {
188:                 self.linear_count += 1;
189:             }
190:             if let Some(val) = self.make_value(typ, port) {
191:                 return Some(val);
192:             }
193:         }
194:     }
195: 
196:     fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
197:         let len = self.types.len() - self.pos;
198:         if self.direction == Direction::Outgoing {
199:             (len, Some(len))
200:         } else {
201:             // Even when yielding every unit, a disconnected input non-linear
202:             // port cannot be assigned a `CircuitUnit::Wire` and so it will be
203:             // skipped.
204:             (0, Some(len))
205:         }
206:     }
207: }

213:     /// Assign a linear unit id to an port.
214:     ///
215:     /// # Parameters

217:     /// - port: The node's port in the node.

219:     fn assign_linear(&self, node: Node, port: Port, linear_count: usize) -> LinearUnit;

223:     /// # Parameters

226:     fn assign_wire(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Wire>;

234: /// An iterator over the commands of a circuit.
235: #[derive(Clone)]
236: pub struct CommandIterator<'circ, Circ> {
237:     /// The circuit.
238:     circ: &'circ Circ,
239:     /// Toposorted nodes.
240:     nodes: NodeWalker,
241:     /// Last wire for each [`LinearUnit`] in the circuit.
242:     wire_unit: HashMap<Wire, usize>,
243:     /// Remaining commands, not counting I/O nodes.
244:     remaining: usize,
245:     /// Delayed output of constant and load const nodes. Contains nodes that
246:     /// haven't been yielded yet.
247:     ///
248:     /// We only yield them as Commands when their consumers require them.
249:     delayed_consts: HashSet<Node>,
250:     /// Nodes with delayed predecessors.
251:     ///
252:     /// Each node is associated with the number of predecessors that are present
253:     /// in `delayed_consts`.
254:     ///
255:     /// This map is used for performance, to avoid checking the neighbours vs
256:     /// the `delayed_consts` set for each processed node.
257:     delayed_consumers: HashMap<Node, usize>,
258:     /// The next node to be processed.
259:     ///
260:     /// This node was produced by the last call to `nodes.next()`, but we had to
261:     /// yield some delayed const nodes before it.
262:     delayed_node: Option<Node>,
263: }
264: 
265: impl<'circ, Circ> CommandIterator<'circ, Circ>
266: where
267:     Circ: Circuit,
268: {
269:     /// Create a new iterator over the commands of a circuit.
270:     pub(super) fn new(circ: &'circ Circ) -> Self {
271:         // Initialize the map assigning linear units to the input's linear
272:         // ports.
273:         //
274:         // TODO: `with_wires` combinator for `Units`?
275:         let wire_unit = circ
276:             .linear_units()
277:             .map(|(linear_unit, port, _)| {
278:                 let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
279:                 (Wire::new(circ.input(), port), linear_unit.index())
280:             })
281:             .collect();
282: 
283:         let nodes = pv::Topo::new(&circ.as_petgraph());
284:         Self {
285:             circ,
286:             nodes,
287:             wire_unit,
288:             // Ignore the input and output nodes, and the root.
289:             remaining: circ.node_count() - 3,
290:             delayed_consts: HashSet::new(),
291:             delayed_consumers: HashMap::new(),
292:             delayed_node: None,
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Returns the next node to be processed.
297:     ///
298:     /// If the next node in the topological order is a constant or load const node,
299:     /// delay it until its consumers are processed.
300:     fn next_node(&mut self) -> Option<Node> {
301:         let node = self
302:             .delayed_node
303:             .take()
304:             .or_else(|| self.nodes.next(&self.circ.as_petgraph()))?;
305: 
306:         // If this node is a constant or load const node, delay it.
307:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
308:         if tag == OpTag::Const || tag == OpTag::LoadConst {
309:             self.delayed_consts.insert(node);
310:             for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(node) {
311:                 *self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer).or_default() += 1;
312:             }
313:             return self.next_node();
314:         }
315: 
316:         // Check if we have any delayed const nodes that are consumed by this node.
317:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&node) {
318:             true => {
319:                 let delayed = self.next_delayed_node(node);
320:                 self.delayed_consts.remove(&delayed);
321:                 for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(delayed) {
322:                     let Entry::Occupied(mut entry) = self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer) else {
323:                         panic!("Delayed node consumer was not in delayed_consumers. Delayed node: {delayed:?}, consumer: {consumer:?}.");
324:                     };
325:                     *entry.get_mut() -= 1;
326:                     if *entry.get() == 0 {
327:                         entry.remove();
328:                     }
329:                 }
330:                 self.delayed_node = Some(node);
331:                 Some(delayed)
332:             }
333:             false => Some(node),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     /// Given a node with delayed predecessors, returns one of those predecessors.
338:     fn next_delayed_node(&mut self, consumer: Node) -> Node {
339:         let Some(delayed_pred) = self
340:             .circ
341:             .input_neighbours(consumer)
342:             .find(|k| self.delayed_consts.contains(k))
343:         else {
344:             panic!("Could not find a delayed predecessor for node {consumer:?}.");
345:         };
346: 
347:         // Only output this node if it doesn't require any other delayed predecessors.
348:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&delayed_pred) {
349:             true => self.next_delayed_node(delayed_pred),
350:             false => delayed_pred,
351:         }
352:     }
353: 
354:     /// Process a new node, updating wires in `unit_wires`.
355:     ///
356:     /// Returns the an option with the `linear_units` used to construct a
357:     /// [`Command`], if the node is not an input or output.
358:     ///
359:     /// We don't return the command directly to avoid lifetime issues due to the
360:     /// mutable borrow here.
361:     fn process_node(&mut self, node: Node) -> Option<Vec<LinearUnit>> {
362:         // The root node is ignored.
363:         if node == self.circ.root() {
364:             return None;
365:         }
366:         // Inputs and outputs are also ignored.
367:         // The input wire ids are already set in the `wire_unit` map during initialization.
368:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
369:         if tag == OpTag::Input || tag == OpTag::Output {
370:             return None;
371:         }
372: 
373:         // Collect the linear units passing through this command into the map
374:         // required to construct a `Command`.
375:         //
376:         // Updates the map tracking the last wire of linear units.
377:         let linear_units: Vec<_> =
378:             Units::new(self.circ, node, Direction::Outgoing, DefaultUnitLabeller)
379:                 .filter_units::<filter::Linear>()
380:                 .map(|(_, port, _)| {
381:                     // Find the linear unit id for this port.
382:                     let linear_id = self
383:                         .follow_linear_port(node, port)
384:                         .and_then(|input_port| {
385:                             let input_port = input_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
386:                             self.circ.linked_outputs(node, input_port).next()
387:                         })
388:                         .and_then(|(from, from_port)| {
389:                             // Remove the old wire from the map (if there was one)
390:                             self.wire_unit.remove(&Wire::new(from, from_port))
391:                         })
392:                         .unwrap_or({
393:                             // New linear unit found. Assign it a new id.
394:                             self.wire_unit.len()
395:                         });
396:                     // Update the map tracking the linear units
397:                     let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
398:                     let new_wire = Wire::new(node, port);
399:                     self.wire_unit.insert(new_wire, linear_id);
400:                     LinearUnit::new(linear_id)
401:                 })
402:                 .collect();
403: 
404:         Some(linear_units)
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Returns the linear port on the node that corresponds to the same linear unit.
408:     ///
409:     /// We assume the linear data uses the same port offsets on both sides of the node.
410:     /// In the future we may want to have a more general mechanism to handle this.
411:     //
412:     // Note that `Command::linear_units` assumes this behaviour.
413:     fn follow_linear_port(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Port> {
414:         let optype = self.circ.get_optype(node);
415:         if !optype.port_kind(port)?.is_linear() {
416:             return None;
417:         }
418:         let other_port = Port::new(port.direction().reverse(), port.index());
419:         if optype.port_kind(other_port) == optype.port_kind(port) {
420:             Some(other_port)
421:         } else {
422:             None
423:         }
424:     }
425: }

434:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
435:         loop {
436:             let node = self.next_node()?;
437:             // Process the node, returning a command if it's not an input or output.
438:             if let Some(linear_units) = self.process_node(node) {
439:                 self.remaining -= 1;
440:                 return Some(Command {
441:                     circ: self.circ,
442:                     node,

445:             }

451:         (self.remaining, Some(self.remaining))

conversation.content:
The current implementation of `op_matches` in `tket2/src/ops.rs` fails to correctly identify custom operations (opaque ops) when matching against known `Tk2Op` variants. This is because it relies on converting the target `Tk2Op` to an extension op and comparing it to the leaf op's extension op — a comparison that fails for `ExternalOp::Opaque` variants.

This issue is causing the hard-coded `AngleAdd` encoder logic in the JSON encoder to not work for `OpaqueOps`. The `record_parameters` function in `tket2/src/json/encoder.rs` checks whether an op matches `Tk2Op::AngleAdd` to handle parameter recording specially, but when the op is represented as an opaque op rather than a resolved extension op, the match fails and the encoder produces incorrect output.

The goal is to fix `op_matches` to correctly identify custom ops by comparing op names rather than relying on resolved extension op equality.

Additionally, while working in the encoder, we should add better error messages for debugging — specifically, give more context in the assertion in `record_parameters` when inputs don't match, and panic with a clear message when encountering non-wire outputs in the parameter recording path.

- Update `op_matches` in `tket2/src/ops.rs` to compare the op name of the given `OpType` against the name of the target `Tk2Op` converted to an `OpType`, rather than comparing extension op instances.
    - Import the `OpName` trait in `tket2/src/ops.rs` to enable the `.name()` method.
    - In `tket2/src/json/encoder.rs`, enhance the debug assertion in `record_parameters` to include information about the found op name, input counts, and node — making failure diagnosis easier.
    - Replace the silent ignore of non-wire outputs in the parameter recording loop with a clear panic that includes the unit and op name, so unexpected cases are surfaced immediately.
    - Run the relevant tests to verify that op detection works for both resolved extension ops and opaque ops, and that the encoder handles `AngleAdd` correctly.

1: //! Intermediate structure for converting encoding [`Circuit`]s into [`SerialCircuit`]s.
2: 
3: use std::collections::HashMap;
4: 
5: use hugr::extension::prelude::QB_T;
6: use hugr::ops::OpType;
7: use hugr::std_extensions::arithmetic::float_types::ConstF64;
8: use hugr::values::Value;
9: use hugr::Wire;
10: use itertools::{Either, Itertools};
11: use tket_json_rs::circuit_json::{self, Permutation, Register, SerialCircuit};
12: 
13: use crate::circuit::command::{CircuitUnit, Command};
14: use crate::circuit::Circuit;
15: use crate::extension::LINEAR_BIT;
16: use crate::ops::{match_symb_const_op, op_matches};
17: use crate::Tk2Op;
18: 
19: use super::op::JsonOp;
20: use super::{
21:     OpConvertError, METADATA_B_REGISTERS, METADATA_IMPLICIT_PERM, METADATA_PHASE,
22:     METADATA_Q_REGISTERS,
23: };
24: 
25: /// The state of an in-progress [`SerialCircuit`] being built from a [`Circuit`].
26: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
27: pub(super) struct JsonEncoder {
28:     /// The name of the circuit being encoded.
29:     name: Option<String>,
30:     /// Global phase value. Defaults to "0"
31:     phase: String,
32:     /// Implicit permutation of output qubits
33:     implicit_permutation: Vec<Permutation>,
34:     /// The current commands
35:     commands: Vec<circuit_json::Command>,
36:     /// The TKET1 qubit registers associated to each qubit unit of the circuit.
37:     qubit_to_reg: HashMap<CircuitUnit, Register>,
38:     /// The TKET1 bit registers associated to each linear bit unit of the circuit.
39:     bit_to_reg: HashMap<CircuitUnit, Register>,
40:     /// The ordered TKET1 names for the input qubit registers.
41:     qubit_registers: Vec<Register>,
42:     /// The ordered TKET1 names for the input bit registers.
43:     bit_registers: Vec<Register>,
44:     /// A register of wires with constant values, used to recover TKET1
45:     /// parameters.
46:     parameters: HashMap<Wire, String>,
47: }
48: 
49: impl JsonEncoder {
50:     /// Create a new [`JsonEncoder`] from a [`Circuit`].
51:     pub fn new(circ: &impl Circuit) -> Self {
52:         let name = circ.name().map(str::to_string);
53: 
54:         let mut qubit_registers = vec![];
55:         let mut bit_registers = vec![];
56:         let mut phase = "0".to_string();
57:         let mut implicit_permutation = vec![];
58: 
59:         // Recover other parameters stored in the metadata
60:         // TODO: Check for invalid encoded metadata
61:         let root = circ.root();
62:         if let Some(p) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_PHASE) {
63:             phase = p.as_str().unwrap().to_string();
64:         }
65:         if let Some(perm) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_IMPLICIT_PERM) {
66:             implicit_permutation = serde_json::from_value(perm.clone()).unwrap();
67:         }
68:         if let Some(q_regs) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_Q_REGISTERS) {
69:             qubit_registers = serde_json::from_value(q_regs.clone()).unwrap();
70:         }
71:         if let Some(b_regs) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_B_REGISTERS) {
72:             bit_registers = serde_json::from_value(b_regs.clone()).unwrap();
73:         }
74: 
75:         // Map the Hugr units to tket1 register names.
76:         // Uses the names from the metadata if available, or initializes new sequentially-numbered registers.
77:         let mut bit_to_reg = HashMap::new();
78:         let mut qubit_to_reg = HashMap::new();
79:         let get_register = |registers: &mut Vec<Register>, prefix: &str, index| {
80:             registers.get(index).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| {
81:                 let r = Register(prefix.to_string(), vec![index as i64]);
82:                 registers.push(r.clone());
83:                 r
84:             })
85:         };
86:         for (unit, _, ty) in circ.units() {
87:             if ty == QB_T {
88:                 let index = qubit_to_reg.len();
89:                 let reg = get_register(&mut qubit_registers, "q", index);
90:                 qubit_to_reg.insert(unit, reg);
91:             } else if ty == *LINEAR_BIT {
92:                 let index = bit_to_reg.len();
93:                 let reg = get_register(&mut bit_registers, "b", index);
94:                 bit_to_reg.insert(unit, reg.clone());
95:             }
96:         }
97: 
98:         Self {
99:             name,
100:             phase,
101:             implicit_permutation,
102:             commands: vec![],
103:             qubit_to_reg,
104:             bit_to_reg,
105:             qubit_registers,
106:             bit_registers,
107:             parameters: HashMap::new(),
108:         }
109:     }
110: 
111:     /// Add a circuit command to the serialization.
112:     pub fn add_command<C: Circuit>(
113:         &mut self,
114:         command: Command<'_, C>,
115:         optype: &OpType,
116:     ) -> Result<(), OpConvertError> {
117:         // Register any output of the command that can be used as a TKET1 parameter.
118:         if self.record_parameters(&command, optype) {
119:             // for now all ops that record parameters should be ignored (are
120:             // just constants)
121:             return Ok(());
122:         }
123: 
124:         let (args, params): (Vec<Register>, Vec<Wire>) =
125:             command
126:                 .inputs()
127:                 .partition_map(|(u, _, _)| match self.unit_to_register(u) {
128:                     Some(r) => Either::Left(r),
129:                     None => match u {
130:                         CircuitUnit::Wire(w) => Either::Right(w),
131:                         CircuitUnit::Linear(_) => {
132:                             panic!("No register found for the linear input {u:?}.")
133:                         }
134:                     },
135:                 });
136: 
137:         // TODO Restore the opgroup (once the decoding supports it)
138:         let opgroup = None;
139:         let op: JsonOp = optype.try_into()?;
140:         let mut op: circuit_json::Operation = op.into_operation();
141:         if !params.is_empty() {
142:             op.params = Some(
143:                 params
144:                     .into_iter()
145:                     .filter_map(|w| self.parameters.get(&w))
146:                     .cloned()
147:                     .collect(),
148:             )
149:         }
150:         // TODO: ops that contain free variables.
151:         // (update decoder to ignore them too, but store them in the wrapped op)
152: 
153:         let command = circuit_json::Command { op, args, opgroup };
154:         self.commands.push(command);
155:         Ok(())
156:     }
157: 
158:     pub fn finish(self) -> SerialCircuit {
159:         SerialCircuit {
160:             name: self.name,
161:             phase: self.phase,
162:             commands: self.commands,
163:             qubits: self.qubit_registers,
164:             bits: self.bit_registers,
165:             implicit_permutation: self.implicit_permutation,
166:         }
167:     }
168: 
169:     /// Record any output of the command that can be used as a TKET1 parameter.
170:     /// Returns whether parameters were recorded.
171:     /// Associates the output wires with the parameter expression.
172:     fn record_parameters<C: Circuit>(&mut self, command: &Command<'_, C>, optype: &OpType) -> bool {
173:         // Only consider commands where all inputs are parameters.
174:         let inputs = command
175:             .inputs()
176:             .filter_map(|(unit, _, _)| match unit {
177:                 CircuitUnit::Wire(wire) => self.parameters.get(&wire),
178:                 CircuitUnit::Linear(_) => None,
179:             })
180:             .collect_vec();
181:         if inputs.len() != command.input_count() {
182:             debug_assert!(!matches!(
183:                 optype,
184:                 OpType::Const(_) | OpType::LoadConstant(_)
185:             ));
186:             return false;
187:         }
188: 
189:         let param = match optype {
190:             OpType::Const(const_op) => {
191:                 // New constant, register it if it can be interpreted as a parameter.
192:                 match const_op.value() {
193:                     Value::Extension { c: (val,) } => {
194:                         if let Some(f) = val.downcast_ref::<ConstF64>() {
195:                             f.to_string()
196:                         } else {
197:                             return false;
198:                         }
199:                     }
200:                     _ => return false,
201:                 }
202:             }
203:             OpType::LoadConstant(_op_type) => {
204:                 // Re-use the parameter from the input.
205:                 inputs[0].clone()
206:             }
207:             op if op_matches(op, Tk2Op::AngleAdd) => {
208:                 format!("{} + {}", inputs[0], inputs[1])
209:             }
210:             OpType::LeafOp(_) => {
211:                 if let Some(s) = match_symb_const_op(optype) {
212:                     s.to_string()
213:                 } else {
214:                     return false;
215:                 }
216:             }
217:             _ => {
218:                 return false;
219:             }
220:         };
221: 
222:         for (unit, _, _) in command.outputs() {
223:             if let CircuitUnit::Wire(wire) = unit {
224:                 self.add_parameter(wire, param.clone());
225:             }
226:         }
227:         true
228:     }
229: 
230:     /// Translate a linear [`CircuitUnit`] into a [`Register`], if possible.
231:     fn unit_to_register(&self, unit: CircuitUnit) -> Option<Register> {
232:         self.qubit_to_reg
233:             .get(&unit)
234:             .or_else(|| self.bit_to_reg.get(&unit))
235:             .cloned()
236:     }
237: 
238:     pub(super) fn add_parameter(&mut self, wire: Wire, param: String) {
239:         self.parameters.insert(wire, param);
240:     }
241: }

268: {
269:     /// Create a new iterator over the commands of a circuit.
270:     pub(super) fn new(circ: &'circ Circ) -> Self {
271:         // Initialize the map assigning linear units to the input's linear
272:         // ports.
273:         //
274:         // TODO: `with_wires` combinator for `Units`?
275:         let wire_unit = circ
276:             .linear_units()
277:             .map(|(linear_unit, port, _)| {
278:                 let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
279:                 (Wire::new(circ.input(), port), linear_unit.index())
280:             })
281:             .collect();
282: 
283:         let nodes = pv::Topo::new(&circ.as_petgraph());
284:         Self {
285:             circ,
286:             nodes,
287:             wire_unit,
288:             // Ignore the input and output nodes, and the root.
289:             remaining: circ.node_count() - 3,
290:             delayed_consts: HashSet::new(),
291:             delayed_consumers: HashMap::new(),
292:             delayed_node: None,
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Returns the next node to be processed.
297:     ///
298:     /// If the next node in the topological order is a constant or load const node,
299:     /// delay it until its consumers are processed.
300:     fn next_node(&mut self) -> Option<Node> {
301:         let node = self
302:             .delayed_node
303:             .take()
304:             .or_else(|| self.nodes.next(&self.circ.as_petgraph()))?;
305: 
306:         // If this node is a constant or load const node, delay it.
307:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
308:         if tag == OpTag::Const || tag == OpTag::LoadConst {
309:             self.delayed_consts.insert(node);
310:             for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(node) {
311:                 *self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer).or_default() += 1;
312:             }
313:             return self.next_node();
314:         }
315: 
316:         // Check if we have any delayed const nodes that are consumed by this node.
317:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&node) {
318:             true => {
319:                 let delayed = self.next_delayed_node(node);
320:                 self.delayed_consts.remove(&delayed);
321:                 for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(delayed) {
322:                     let Entry::Occupied(mut entry) = self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer) else {
323:                         panic!("Delayed node consumer was not in delayed_consumers. Delayed node: {delayed:?}, consumer: {consumer:?}.");
324:                     };
325:                     *entry.get_mut() -= 1;
326:                     if *entry.get() == 0 {
327:                         entry.remove();
328:                     }
329:                 }
330:                 self.delayed_node = Some(node);
331:                 Some(delayed)
332:             }
333:             false => Some(node),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     /// Given a node with delayed predecessors, returns one of those predecessors.
338:     fn next_delayed_node(&mut self, consumer: Node) -> Node {
339:         let Some(delayed_pred) = self
340:             .circ
341:             .input_neighbours(consumer)
342:             .find(|k| self.delayed_consts.contains(k))
343:         else {
344:             panic!("Could not find a delayed predecessor for node {consumer:?}.");
345:         };
346: 
347:         // Only output this node if it doesn't require any other delayed predecessors.
348:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&delayed_pred) {
349:             true => self.next_delayed_node(delayed_pred),
350:             false => delayed_pred,
351:         }
352:     }

354:     /// Process a new node, updating wires in `unit_wires`.
355:     ///
356:     /// Returns the an option with the `linear_units` used to construct a
357:     /// [`Command`], if the node is not an input or output.
358:     ///
359:     /// We don't return the command directly to avoid lifetime issues due to the
360:     /// mutable borrow here.
361:     fn process_node(&mut self, node: Node) -> Option<Vec<LinearUnit>> {
362:         // The root node is ignored.
363:         if node == self.circ.root() {
364:             return None;
365:         }
366:         // Inputs and outputs are also ignored.
367:         // The input wire ids are already set in the `wire_unit` map during initialization.
368:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
369:         if tag == OpTag::Input || tag == OpTag::Output {
370:             return None;
371:         }
372: 
373:         // Collect the linear units passing through this command into the map
374:         // required to construct a `Command`.
375:         //
376:         // Updates the map tracking the last wire of linear units.
377:         let linear_units: Vec<_> =
378:             Units::new(self.circ, node, Direction::Outgoing, DefaultUnitLabeller)
379:                 .filter_units::<filter::Linear>()
380:                 .map(|(_, port, _)| {
381:                     // Find the linear unit id for this port.
382:                     let linear_id = self
383:                         .follow_linear_port(node, port)
384:                         .and_then(|input_port| {
385:                             let input_port = input_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
386:                             self.circ.linked_outputs(node, input_port).next()
387:                         })
388:                         .and_then(|(from, from_port)| {
389:                             // Remove the old wire from the map (if there was one)
390:                             self.wire_unit.remove(&Wire::new(from, from_port))
391:                         })
392:                         .unwrap_or({
393:                             // New linear unit found. Assign it a new id.
394:                             self.wire_unit.len()
395:                         });
396:                     // Update the map tracking the linear units
397:                     let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
398:                     let new_wire = Wire::new(node, port);
399:                     self.wire_unit.insert(new_wire, linear_id);
400:                     LinearUnit::new(linear_id)
401:                 })
402:                 .collect();
403: 
404:         Some(linear_units)
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Returns the linear port on the node that corresponds to the same linear unit.
408:     ///
409:     /// We assume the linear data uses the same port offsets on both sides of the node.
410:     /// In the future we may want to have a more general mechanism to handle this.
411:     //
412:     // Note that `Command::linear_units` assumes this behaviour.
413:     fn follow_linear_port(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Port> {
414:         let optype = self.circ.get_optype(node);
415:         if !optype.port_kind(port)?.is_linear() {
416:             return None;
417:         }
418:         let other_port = Port::new(port.direction().reverse(), port.index());
419:         if optype.port_kind(other_port) == optype.port_kind(port) {
420:             Some(other_port)
421:         } else {
422:             None
423:         }
424:     }
425: }

25: /// The state of an in-progress [`SerialCircuit`] being built from a [`Circuit`].
26: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
27: pub(super) struct JsonEncoder {
28:     /// The name of the circuit being encoded.
29:     name: Option<String>,
30:     /// Global phase value. Defaults to "0"
31:     phase: String,
32:     /// Implicit permutation of output qubits
33:     implicit_permutation: Vec<Permutation>,
34:     /// The current commands
35:     commands: Vec<circuit_json::Command>,
36:     /// The TKET1 qubit registers associated to each qubit unit of the circuit.
37:     qubit_to_reg: HashMap<CircuitUnit, Register>,
38:     /// The TKET1 bit registers associated to each linear bit unit of the circuit.
39:     bit_to_reg: HashMap<CircuitUnit, Register>,
40:     /// The ordered TKET1 names for the input qubit registers.
41:     qubit_registers: Vec<Register>,
42:     /// The ordered TKET1 names for the input bit registers.
43:     bit_registers: Vec<Register>,
44:     /// A register of wires with constant values, used to recover TKET1
45:     /// parameters.
46:     parameters: HashMap<Wire, String>,
47: }

49: impl JsonEncoder {
50:     /// Create a new [`JsonEncoder`] from a [`Circuit`].
51:     pub fn new(circ: &impl Circuit) -> Self {
52:         let name = circ.name().map(str::to_string);
53: 
54:         let mut qubit_registers = vec![];
55:         let mut bit_registers = vec![];
56:         let mut phase = "0".to_string();
57:         let mut implicit_permutation = vec![];
58: 
59:         // Recover other parameters stored in the metadata
60:         // TODO: Check for invalid encoded metadata
61:         let root = circ.root();
62:         if let Some(p) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_PHASE) {
63:             phase = p.as_str().unwrap().to_string();
64:         }
65:         if let Some(perm) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_IMPLICIT_PERM) {
66:             implicit_permutation = serde_json::from_value(perm.clone()).unwrap();
67:         }
68:         if let Some(q_regs) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_Q_REGISTERS) {
69:             qubit_registers = serde_json::from_value(q_regs.clone()).unwrap();
70:         }
71:         if let Some(b_regs) = circ.get_metadata(root, METADATA_B_REGISTERS) {
72:             bit_registers = serde_json::from_value(b_regs.clone()).unwrap();
73:         }
74: 
75:         // Map the Hugr units to tket1 register names.
76:         // Uses the names from the metadata if available, or initializes new sequentially-numbered registers.
77:         let mut bit_to_reg = HashMap::new();
78:         let mut qubit_to_reg = HashMap::new();
79:         let get_register = |registers: &mut Vec<Register>, prefix: &str, index| {
80:             registers.get(index).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| {
81:                 let r = Register(prefix.to_string(), vec![index as i64]);
82:                 registers.push(r.clone());
83:                 r
84:             })
85:         };
86:         for (unit, _, ty) in circ.units() {
87:             if ty == QB_T {
88:                 let index = qubit_to_reg.len();
89:                 let reg = get_register(&mut qubit_registers, "q", index);
90:                 qubit_to_reg.insert(unit, reg);
91:             } else if ty == *LINEAR_BIT {
92:                 let index = bit_to_reg.len();
93:                 let reg = get_register(&mut bit_registers, "b", index);
94:                 bit_to_reg.insert(unit, reg.clone());
95:             }
96:         }
97: 
98:         Self {
99:             name,
100:             phase,
101:             implicit_permutation,
102:             commands: vec![],
103:             qubit_to_reg,
104:             bit_to_reg,
105:             qubit_registers,
106:             bit_registers,
107:             parameters: HashMap::new(),
108:         }
109:     }

111:     /// Add a circuit command to the serialization.
112:     pub fn add_command<C: Circuit>(

116:     ) -> Result<(), OpConvertError> {

118:         if self.record_parameters(&command, optype) {

173:         // Only consider commands where all inputs are parameters.
174:         let inputs = command
175:             .inputs()

226:         for (unit, _, _) in command.outputs() {
227:             match unit {

1: //! This module defines the internal `JsonOp` struct wrapping the logic for
2: //! going between `tket_json_rs::optype::OpType` and `hugr::ops::OpType`.
3: //!
4: //! The `JsonOp` tries to homogenize the
5: //! `tket_json_rs::circuit_json::Operation`s coming from the encoded TKET1
6: //! circuits by ensuring they always define a signature, and computing the
7: //! explicit count of qubits and linear bits.
8: 
9: use hugr::extension::prelude::QB_T;
10: 
11: use hugr::ops::custom::ExternalOp;
12: use hugr::ops::{LeafOp, OpTrait, OpType};
13: use hugr::std_extensions::arithmetic::float_types::FLOAT64_TYPE;
14: use hugr::types::FunctionType;
15: 
16: use itertools::Itertools;
17: use tket_json_rs::circuit_json;
18: use tket_json_rs::optype::OpType as JsonOpType;
19: 
20: use super::OpConvertError;
21: use crate::extension::{try_unwrap_json_op, LINEAR_BIT};
22: use crate::Tk2Op;
23: 
24: /// A serialized operation, containing the operation type and all its attributes.
25: ///
26: /// Wrapper around [`circuit_json::Operation`] with cached number of qubits and bits.
27: ///
28: /// The `Operation` contained by this struct is guaranteed to have a signature.
29: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
30: pub(crate) struct JsonOp {
31:     op: circuit_json::Operation,
32:     num_qubits: usize,
33:     num_bits: usize,
34:     /// Node input for each parameter in `op.params`.
35:     ///
36:     /// If the input is `None`, the parameter does not use a Hugr port and is
37:     /// instead stored purely as metadata for the `Operation`.
38:     param_inputs: Vec<Option<usize>>,
39:     /// The number of non-None inputs in `param_inputs`, corresponding to the
40:     /// FLOAT64_TYPE inputs to the Hugr operation.
41:     num_params: usize,
42: }
43: 
44: impl JsonOp {
45:     /// Create a new `JsonOp` from a `circuit_json::Operation`, computing its
46:     /// number of qubits from the signature
47:     ///
48:     /// Fails if the operation does not define a signature. See
49:     /// [`JsonOp::new_from_op`] for a version that generates a signature if none
50:     /// is defined.
51:     #[allow(unused)]
52:     pub fn new(op: circuit_json::Operation) -> Option<Self> {
53:         let Some(sig) = &op.signature else {
54:             return None;
55:         };
56:         let input_counts = sig.iter().map(String::as_ref).counts();
57:         let num_qubits = input_counts.get("Q").copied().unwrap_or(0);
58:         let num_bits = input_counts.get("B").copied().unwrap_or(0);
59:         let mut op = Self {
60:             op,
61:             num_qubits,
62:             num_bits,
63:             param_inputs: Vec::new(),
64:             num_params: 0,
65:         };
66:         op.compute_param_fields();
67:         Some(op)
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// Create a new `JsonOp` from a `circuit_json::Operation`, with the number
71:     /// of qubits and bits explicitly specified.
72:     ///
73:     /// If the operation does not define a signature, one is generated with the
74:     /// given amounts.
75:     pub fn new_from_op(
76:         mut op: circuit_json::Operation,
77:         num_qubits: usize,
78:         num_bits: usize,
79:     ) -> Self {
80:         if op.signature.is_none() {
81:             op.signature =
82:                 Some([vec!["Q".into(); num_qubits], vec!["B".into(); num_bits]].concat());
83:         }
84:         let mut op = Self {
85:             op,
86:             num_qubits,
87:             num_bits,
88:             param_inputs: Vec::new(),
89:             num_params: 0,
90:         };
91:         op.compute_param_fields();
92:         op
93:     }
94: 
95:     /// Create a new `JsonOp` from the optype and the number of parameters.
96:     pub fn new_with_counts(
97:         json_optype: JsonOpType,
98:         num_qubits: usize,
99:         num_bits: usize,
100:         num_params: usize,
101:     ) -> Self {
102:         let mut params = None;
103:         let mut param_inputs = vec![];
104:         if num_params > 0 {
105:             let offset = num_qubits + num_bits;
106:             params = Some(vec!["".into(); num_params]);
107:             param_inputs = (offset..offset + num_params).map(Option::Some).collect();
108:         }
109:         let op = circuit_json::Operation {
110:             op_type: json_optype,
111:             n_qb: Some(num_qubits as u32),
112:             params,
113:             op_box: None,
114:             signature: Some([vec!["Q".into(); num_qubits], vec!["B".into(); num_bits]].concat()),
115:             conditional: None,
116:         };
117:         Self {
118:             op,
119:             num_qubits,
120:             num_bits,
121:             param_inputs,
122:             num_params,
123:         }
124:     }
125: 
126:     /// Compute the signature of the operation.
127:     #[inline]
128:     pub fn signature(&self) -> FunctionType {
129:         let linear = [
130:             vec![QB_T; self.num_qubits],
131:             vec![LINEAR_BIT.clone(); self.num_bits],
132:         ]
133:         .concat();
134:         let params = vec![FLOAT64_TYPE; self.num_params];
135:         FunctionType::new([linear.clone(), params].concat(), linear)
136:         // .with_extension_delta(&ExtensionSet::singleton(&TKET1_EXTENSION_ID))
137:     }
138: 
139:     /// List of parameters in the operation that should be exposed as inputs.
140:     #[inline]
141:     pub fn param_inputs(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
142:         self.param_inputs
143:             .iter()
144:             .filter_map(|&i| self.op.params.as_ref()?.get(i?).map(String::as_ref))
145:     }
146: 
147:     pub fn into_operation(self) -> circuit_json::Operation {
148:         self.op
149:     }
150: 
151:     /// Wraps the op into a Hugr opaque operation
152:     fn as_opaque_op(&self) -> ExternalOp {
153:         crate::extension::wrap_json_op(self)
154:     }
155: 
156:     /// Compute the `parameter_input` and `num_params` fields by looking for
157:     /// parameters in `op.params` that can be mapped to input wires in the Hugr.
158:     ///
159:     /// Updates the internal `num_params` and `param_inputs` fields.
160:     fn compute_param_fields(&mut self) {
161:         let Some(params) = self.op.params.as_ref() else {
162:             self.param_inputs = vec![];
163:             self.num_params = 0;
164:             return;
165:         };
166: 
167:         self.num_params = params.len();
168:         self.param_inputs = (0..params.len()).map(Some).collect();
169:     }
170: }

172: impl From<&JsonOp> for OpType {
173:     /// Convert the operation into a HUGR operation.
174:     ///
175:     /// We only translate operations that have a 1:1 mapping between TKET and HUGR.
176:     /// Any other operation is wrapped in an `OpaqueOp`.
177:     fn from(json_op: &JsonOp) -> Self {
178:         match json_op.op.op_type {
179:             // JsonOpType::X => LeafOp::X.into(),
180:             JsonOpType::H => Tk2Op::H.into(),
181:             JsonOpType::CX => Tk2Op::CX.into(),
182:             JsonOpType::T => Tk2Op::T.into(),
183:             JsonOpType::Tdg => Tk2Op::Tdg.into(),
184:             JsonOpType::X => Tk2Op::X.into(),
185:             JsonOpType::Y => Tk2Op::Y.into(),
186:             JsonOpType::Z => Tk2Op::Z.into(),
187:             JsonOpType::Rz => Tk2Op::RzF64.into(),
188:             JsonOpType::Rx => Tk2Op::RxF64.into(),
189:             JsonOpType::TK1 => Tk2Op::TK1.into(),
190:             JsonOpType::PhasedX => Tk2Op::PhasedX.into(),
191:             JsonOpType::ZZMax => Tk2Op::ZZMax.into(),
192:             JsonOpType::ZZPhase => Tk2Op::ZZPhase.into(),
193:             JsonOpType::CZ => Tk2Op::CZ.into(),
194:             JsonOpType::noop => LeafOp::Noop { ty: QB_T }.into(),
195:             _ => LeafOp::CustomOp(Box::new(json_op.as_opaque_op())).into(),
196:         }
197:     }
198: }
199: 
200: impl TryFrom<&OpType> for JsonOp {
201:     type Error = OpConvertError;
202: 
203:     fn try_from(op: &OpType) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
204:         // We only translate operations that have a 1:1 mapping between TKET and TKET2
205:         //
206:         // Other TKET1 operations are wrapped in an `OpaqueOp`.
207:         //
208:         // Non-supported Hugr operations throw an error.
209:         let err = || OpConvertError::UnsupportedOpSerialization(op.clone());
210:         let Some(leaf) = op.as_leaf_op() else {
211:             return Err(err());
212:         };
213: 
214:         let json_optype = if let Ok(tk2op) = leaf.try_into() {
215:             match tk2op {
216:                 Tk2Op::H => JsonOpType::H,
217:                 Tk2Op::CX => JsonOpType::CX,
218:                 Tk2Op::T => JsonOpType::T,
219:                 Tk2Op::S => JsonOpType::S,
220:                 Tk2Op::X => JsonOpType::X,
221:                 Tk2Op::Y => JsonOpType::Y,
222:                 Tk2Op::Z => JsonOpType::Z,
223:                 Tk2Op::Tdg => JsonOpType::Tdg,
224:                 Tk2Op::Sdg => JsonOpType::Sdg,
225:                 Tk2Op::ZZMax => JsonOpType::ZZMax,
226:                 Tk2Op::Measure => JsonOpType::Measure,
227:                 Tk2Op::RzF64 => JsonOpType::Rz,
228:                 Tk2Op::RxF64 => JsonOpType::Rx,
229:                 // TODO: Use a TK2 opaque op once we update the tket-json-rs dependency.
230:                 Tk2Op::AngleAdd => {
231:                     unimplemented!("Serialising AngleAdd not supported. Are all constant folded?")
232:                 }
233:                 Tk2Op::TK1 => JsonOpType::TK1,
234:                 Tk2Op::PhasedX => JsonOpType::PhasedX,
235:                 Tk2Op::ZZPhase => JsonOpType::ZZPhase,
236:                 Tk2Op::CZ => JsonOpType::CZ,
237:             }
238:         } else if let LeafOp::CustomOp(b) = leaf {
239:             let ext = (*b).as_ref();
240:             return try_unwrap_json_op(ext).ok_or_else(err);
241:         } else {
242:             return Err(err());
243:         };
244: 
245:         let mut num_qubits = 0;
246:         let mut num_bits = 0;
247:         let mut num_params = 0;
248:         if let Some(sig) = op.dataflow_signature() {
249:             for ty in sig.input.iter() {
250:                 if ty == &QB_T {
251:                     num_qubits += 1
252:                 } else if *ty == *LINEAR_BIT {
253:                     num_bits += 1
254:                 } else if ty == &FLOAT64_TYPE {
255:                     num_params += 1
256:                 }
257:             }
258:         }
259: 
260:         Ok(JsonOp::new_with_counts(
261:             json_optype,
262:             num_qubits,
263:             num_bits,
264:             num_params,
265:         ))
266:     }
267: }

98: impl<UL> Units<UL>
99: where
100:     UL: UnitLabeller,
101: {
102:     /// Apply a [`UnitFilter`] to the iterator's output, possibly unwrapping the
103:     /// [`CircuitUnit`] into either a linear unit or a wire.
104:     pub fn filter_units<F: UnitFilter>(self) -> FilteredUnits<F, UL> {
105:         self.filter_map(F::accept)
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Create a new iterator over the units of a node.
109:     //
110:     // Note that this ignores any incoming linear unit labels, and just assigns
111:     // new unit ids sequentially.
112:     #[inline]
113:     pub(super) fn new(
114:         circuit: &impl Circuit,
115:         node: Node,
116:         direction: Direction,
117:         unit_labeller: UL,
118:     ) -> Self {
119:         Self {
120:             node,
121:             direction,
122:             types: Self::init_types(circuit, node, direction),
123:             pos: 0,
124:             linear_count: 0,
125:             unit_labeller,
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Initialize the boundary types.
130:     ///
131:     /// We use a [`TypeRow`] to avoid allocating for simple boundaries, but if
132:     /// any static port is present we create a new owned [`TypeRow`] with them included.
133:     //
134:     // TODO: This is quite hacky, but we need it to accept Const static inputs.
135:     // We should revisit it once this is reworked on the HUGR side.
136:     fn init_types(circuit: &impl Circuit, node: Node, direction: Direction) -> TypeRow {
137:         let optype = circuit.get_optype(node);
138:         let sig = circuit.signature(node).unwrap_or_default();
139:         let mut types = match direction {
140:             Direction::Outgoing => sig.output,
141:             Direction::Incoming => sig.input,
142:         };
143:         if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(static_type)) = optype.static_port_kind(direction) {
144:             types.to_mut().push(static_type);
145:         };
146:         if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(other)) = optype.other_port_kind(direction) {
147:             types.to_mut().push(other);
148:         }
149:         types
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Construct an output value to yield.
153:     ///
154:     /// Calls [`UnitLabeller::assign_linear`] to assign a linear unit id to the linear ports.
155:     /// Non-linear ports are assigned [`CircuitUnit::Wire`]s via [`UnitLabeller::assign_wire`].
156:     #[inline]
157:     fn make_value(&self, typ: &Type, port: Port) -> Option<(CircuitUnit, Port, Type)> {
158:         let unit = if type_is_linear(typ) {
159:             let linear_unit =
160:                 self.unit_labeller
161:                     .assign_linear(self.node, port, self.linear_count - 1);
162:             CircuitUnit::Linear(linear_unit.index())
163:         } else {
164:             let wire = self.unit_labeller.assign_wire(self.node, port)?;
165:             CircuitUnit::Wire(wire)
166:         };
167:         Some((unit, port, typ.clone()))
168:     }
169: }
170: 
171: impl<UL> Iterator for Units<UL>
172: where
173:     UL: UnitLabeller,
174: {
175:     type Item = (CircuitUnit, Port, Type);
176: 
177:     #[inline]
178:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
179:         loop {
180:             let typ = self.types.get(self.pos)?;
181:             let port = Port::new(self.direction, self.pos);
182:             self.pos += 1;
183:             if type_is_linear(typ) {
184:                 self.linear_count += 1;
185:             }
186:             if let Some(val) = self.make_value(typ, port) {
187:                 return Some(val);
188:             }
189:         }
190:     }
191: 
192:     fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
193:         let len = self.types.len() - self.pos;
194:         if self.direction == Direction::Outgoing {
195:             (len, Some(len))
196:         } else {
197:             // Even when yielding every unit, a disconnected input non-linear
198:             // port cannot be assigned a `CircuitUnit::Wire` and so it will be
199:             // skipped.
200:             (0, Some(len))
201:         }
202:     }
203: }

205: impl<UL> FusedIterator for Units<UL> where UL: UnitLabeller {}

232: type NodeWalker = pv::Topo<Node, HashSet<Node>>;
