234: /// An iterator over the commands of a circuit.
235: #[derive(Clone)]
236: pub struct CommandIterator<'circ, Circ> {
237:     /// The circuit.
238:     circ: &'circ Circ,
239:     /// Toposorted nodes.
240:     nodes: NodeWalker,
241:     /// Last wire for each [`LinearUnit`] in the circuit.
242:     wire_unit: HashMap<Wire, usize>,
243:     /// Remaining commands, not counting I/O nodes.
244:     remaining: usize,
245:     /// Delayed output of constant and load const nodes. Contains nodes that
246:     /// haven't been yielded yet.
247:     ///
248:     /// We only yield them as Commands when their consumers require them.
249:     delayed_consts: HashSet<Node>,
250:     /// Nodes with delayed predecessors.
251:     ///
252:     /// Each node is associated with the number of predecessors that are present
253:     /// in `delayed_consts`.
254:     ///
255:     /// This map is used for performance, to avoid checking the neighbours vs
256:     /// the `delayed_consts` set for each processed node.
257:     delayed_consumers: HashMap<Node, usize>,
258:     /// The next node to be processed.
259:     ///
260:     /// This node was produced by the last call to `nodes.next()`, but we had to
261:     /// yield some delayed const nodes before it.
262:     delayed_node: Option<Node>,
263: }
264: 
265: impl<'circ, Circ> CommandIterator<'circ, Circ>
266: where
267:     Circ: Circuit,
268: {
269:     /// Create a new iterator over the commands of a circuit.
270:     pub(super) fn new(circ: &'circ Circ) -> Self {
271:         // Initialize the map assigning linear units to the input's linear
272:         // ports.
273:         //
274:         // TODO: `with_wires` combinator for `Units`?
275:         let wire_unit = circ
276:             .linear_units()
277:             .map(|(linear_unit, port, _)| {
278:                 let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
279:                 (Wire::new(circ.input(), port), linear_unit.index())
280:             })
281:             .collect();
282: 
283:         let nodes = pv::Topo::new(&circ.as_petgraph());
284:         Self {
285:             circ,
286:             nodes,
287:             wire_unit,
288:             // Ignore the input and output nodes, and the root.
289:             remaining: circ.node_count() - 3,
290:             delayed_consts: HashSet::new(),
291:             delayed_consumers: HashMap::new(),
292:             delayed_node: None,
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Returns the next node to be processed.
297:     ///
298:     /// If the next node in the topological order is a constant or load const node,
299:     /// delay it until its consumers are processed.
300:     fn next_node(&mut self) -> Option<Node> {
301:         let node = self
302:             .delayed_node
303:             .take()
304:             .or_else(|| self.nodes.next(&self.circ.as_petgraph()))?;
305: 
306:         // If this node is a constant or load const node, delay it.
307:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
308:         if tag == OpTag::Const || tag == OpTag::LoadConst {
309:             self.delayed_consts.insert(node);
310:             for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(node) {
311:                 *self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer).or_default() += 1;
312:             }
313:             return self.next_node();
314:         }
315: 
316:         // Check if we have any delayed const nodes that are consumed by this node.
317:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&node) {
318:             true => {
319:                 let delayed = self.next_delayed_node(node);
320:                 self.delayed_consts.remove(&delayed);
321:                 for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(delayed) {
322:                     let Entry::Occupied(mut entry) = self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer) else {
323:                         panic!("Delayed node consumer was not in delayed_consumers. Delayed node: {delayed:?}, consumer: {consumer:?}.");
324:                     };
325:                     *entry.get_mut() -= 1;
326:                     if *entry.get() == 0 {
327:                         entry.remove();
328:                     }
329:                 }
330:                 self.delayed_node = Some(node);
331:                 Some(delayed)
332:             }
333:             false => Some(node),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     /// Given a node with delayed predecessors, returns one of those predecessors.
338:     fn next_delayed_node(&mut self, consumer: Node) -> Node {
339:         let Some(delayed_pred) = self
340:             .circ
341:             .input_neighbours(consumer)
342:             .find(|k| self.delayed_consts.contains(k))
343:         else {
344:             panic!("Could not find a delayed predecessor for node {consumer:?}.");
345:         };
346: 
347:         // Only output this node if it doesn't require any other delayed predecessors.
348:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&delayed_pred) {
349:             true => self.next_delayed_node(delayed_pred),
350:             false => delayed_pred,
351:         }
352:     }
353: 
354:     /// Process a new node, updating wires in `unit_wires`.
355:     ///
356:     /// Returns the an option with the `linear_units` used to construct a
357:     /// [`Command`], if the node is not an input or output.
358:     ///
359:     /// We don't return the command directly to avoid lifetime issues due to the
360:     /// mutable borrow here.
361:     fn process_node(&mut self, node: Node) -> Option<Vec<LinearUnit>> {
362:         // The root node is ignored.
363:         if node == self.circ.root() {
364:             return None;
365:         }
366:         // Inputs and outputs are also ignored.
367:         // The input wire ids are already set in the `wire_unit` map during initialization.
368:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
369:         if tag == OpTag::Input || tag == OpTag::Output {
370:             return None;
371:         }
372: 
373:         // Collect the linear units passing through this command into the map
374:         // required to construct a `Command`.
375:         //
376:         // Updates the map tracking the last wire of linear units.
377:         let linear_units: Vec<_> =
378:             Units::new(self.circ, node, Direction::Outgoing, DefaultUnitLabeller)
379:                 .filter_units::<filter::Linear>()
380:                 .map(|(_, port, _)| {
381:                     // Find the linear unit id for this port.
382:                     let linear_id = self
383:                         .follow_linear_port(node, port)
384:                         .and_then(|input_port| {
385:                             let input_port = input_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
386:                             self.circ.linked_outputs(node, input_port).next()
387:                         })
388:                         .and_then(|(from, from_port)| {
389:                             // Remove the old wire from the map (if there was one)
390:                             self.wire_unit.remove(&Wire::new(from, from_port))
391:                         })
392:                         .unwrap_or({
393:                             // New linear unit found. Assign it a new id.
394:                             self.wire_unit.len()
395:                         });
396:                     // Update the map tracking the linear units
397:                     let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
398:                     let new_wire = Wire::new(node, port);
399:                     self.wire_unit.insert(new_wire, linear_id);
400:                     LinearUnit::new(linear_id)
401:                 })
402:                 .collect();
403: 
404:         Some(linear_units)
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Returns the linear port on the node that corresponds to the same linear unit.
408:     ///
409:     /// We assume the linear data uses the same port offsets on both sides of the node.
410:     /// In the future we may want to have a more general mechanism to handle this.
411:     //
412:     // Note that `Command::linear_units` assumes this behaviour.
413:     fn follow_linear_port(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Port> {
414:         let optype = self.circ.get_optype(node);
415:         if !optype.port_kind(port)?.is_linear() {
416:             return None;
417:         }
418:         let other_port = Port::new(port.direction().reverse(), port.index());
419:         if optype.port_kind(other_port) == optype.port_kind(port) {
420:             Some(other_port)
421:         } else {
422:             None
423:         }
424:     }
425: }

73:     /// # Errors

77:         &mut self,

106: /// Starting from starting_index, work back along slices to check for the
107: /// earliest slice that can accommodate this command, if any.
108: fn available_slice(
109:     circ: &impl HugrView,
110:     slice_vec: &[Slice],
111:     starting_index: usize,
112:     command: &Rc<ComCommand>,
113: ) -> Option<(usize, HashMap<Qb, Rc<ComCommand>>)> {
114:     let mut available = None;
115:     let mut prev_nodes: HashMap<Qb, Rc<ComCommand>> = HashMap::new();
116:     for slice_index in (0..=starting_index).rev() {
117:         // if all qubit slots are empty here the command can be moved here
118:         if command
119:             .qubits()
120:             .all(|q| slice_vec[slice_index][q.index()].is_none())
121:         {
122:             available = Some((slice_index, prev_nodes.clone()));
123:         } else if slice_index == 0 {
124:             break;
125:         } else {
126:             // if command commutes with all ports here it can be moved past,
127:             // otherwise stop
128:             if let Some(new_prev_nodes) = commutes_at_slice(command, &slice_vec[slice_index], circ)
129:             {
130:                 prev_nodes.extend(new_prev_nodes);
131:             } else {
132:                 break;
133:             }
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     available
138: }

140: // If a command commutes back through this slice return a map from the qubits of
141: // the command to the commands in this slice acting on those qubits.
142: fn commutes_at_slice(
143:     command: &Rc<ComCommand>,
144:     slice: &Slice,
145:     circ: &impl HugrView,
146: ) -> Option<HashMap<Qb, Rc<ComCommand>>> {
147:     // map from qubit to node it is connected to immediately after the free slice.
148:     let mut prev_nodes: HashMap<Qb, Rc<ComCommand>> = HashMap::new();
149: 
150:     for q in command.qubits() {
151:         // if slot is empty, continue checking.
152:         let Some(other_com) = &slice[q.index()] else {
153:             continue;
154:         };
155: 
156:         let port = command.port_of_qb(q, Direction::Incoming)?;
157: 
158:         let op: Tk2Op = circ.get_optype(command.node()).clone().try_into().ok()?;
159:         // TODO: if not tk2op, might still have serialized commutation data we
160:         // can use.
161:         let pauli = commutation_on_port(&op.qubit_commutation(), port)?;
162: 
163:         let other_op: Tk2Op = circ.get_optype(other_com.node()).clone().try_into().ok()?;
164:         let other_pauli = commutation_on_port(
165:             &other_op.qubit_commutation(),
166:             other_com.port_of_qb(q, Direction::Outgoing)?,
167:         )?;
168: 
169:         if pauli.commutes_with(other_pauli) {
170:             prev_nodes.insert(q, other_com.clone());
171:         } else {
172:             return None;
173:         }
174:     }
175: 
176:     Some(prev_nodes)
177: }

179: fn commutation_on_port(comms: &[(usize, Pauli)], port: Port) -> Option<Pauli> {
180:     comms
181:         .iter()
182:         .find_map(|(i, p)| (*i == port.index()).then_some(*p))
183: }

185: /// Error from a `PullForward` operation.
186: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
187: #[allow(missing_docs)]
188: pub enum PullForwardError {
189:     // Error in hugr mutation.
190:     #[error("Hugr mutation error: {0:?}")]
191:     HugrError(#[from] HugrError),
192: 
193:     #[error("Qubit {0} not found in command.")]
194:     NoQbInCommand(usize),
195: 
196:     #[error("No subsequent command found for qubit {0}")]
197:     NoCommandForQb(usize),
198: }

200: struct PullForward {
201:     command: Rc<ComCommand>,
202:     new_nexts: HashMap<Qb, Rc<ComCommand>>,
203: }
204: 
205: impl Rewrite for PullForward {
206:     type Error = PullForwardError;
207: 
208:     type ApplyResult = ();
209: 
210:     type InvalidationSet<'a> = std::vec::IntoIter<Node>
211:     where
212:         Self: 'a;
213: 
214:     const UNCHANGED_ON_FAILURE: bool = false;
215: 
216:     fn verify(&self, _h: &impl HugrView) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
217:         unimplemented!()
218:     }
219: 
220:     fn apply(self, h: &mut impl HugrMut) -> Result<Self::ApplyResult, Self::Error> {
221:         let Self { command, new_nexts } = self;
222: 
223:         let qb_port = |command: &ComCommand, qb, direction| {
224:             command
225:                 .port_of_qb(qb, direction)
226:                 .ok_or(PullForwardError::NoQbInCommand(qb.index()))
227:         };
228:         // for each qubit, disconnect node and reconnect at destination.
229:         for qb in command.qubits() {
230:             let out_port = qb_port(&command, qb, Direction::Outgoing)?;
231:             let in_port = qb_port(&command, qb, Direction::Incoming)?;
232: 
233:             let (src, src_port) = h
234:                 .linked_ports(command.node(), in_port)
235:                 .exactly_one()
236:                 .ok() // PortLinks don't implement Debug
237:                 .unwrap();
238:             let (dst, dst_port) = h
239:                 .linked_ports(command.node(), out_port)
240:                 .exactly_one()
241:                 .ok()
242:                 .unwrap();
243: 
244:             let Some(new_neighbour_com) = new_nexts.get(&qb) else {
245:                 return Err(PullForwardError::NoCommandForQb(qb.index()));
246:             };
247:             if new_neighbour_com == &command {
248:                 // do not need to commute along this qubit.
249:                 continue;
250:             }
251:             h.disconnect(command.node(), in_port)?;
252:             h.disconnect(command.node(), out_port)?;
253:             // connect old source and destination - identity operation.
254:             h.connect(src, src_port.index(), dst, dst_port.index())?;
255: 
256:             let new_dst_port = qb_port(new_neighbour_com, qb, Direction::Incoming)?;
257:             let (new_src, new_src_port) = h
258:                 .linked_ports(new_neighbour_com.node(), new_dst_port)
259:                 .exactly_one()
260:                 .ok()
261:                 .unwrap();
262:             // disconnect link which we will insert in to.
263:             h.disconnect(new_neighbour_com.node(), new_dst_port)?;
264: 
265:             h.connect(
266:                 new_src,
267:                 new_src_port.index(),
268:                 command.node(),
269:                 in_port.index(),
270:             )?;
271:             h.connect(
272:                 command.node(),
273:                 out_port.index(),
274:                 new_neighbour_com.node(),
275:                 new_dst_port.index(),
276:             )?;
277:         }
278:         Ok(())
279:     }

281:     fn invalidation_set(&self) -> Self::InvalidationSet<'_> {
282:         // TODO: This could avoid creating a vec, but it'll be easier to do once
283:         // return position impl trait is available.
284:         let mut nodes = vec![self.command.node()];
285:         let next_nodes = self.new_nexts.values().map(|c| c.node());
286:         nodes.extend(next_nodes);
287:         nodes.into_iter()
288:     }
289: }

291: /// Pass which greedily commutes operations forwards in order to reduce depth.
292: pub fn apply_greedy_commutation(circ: &mut Hugr) -> Result<u32, PullForwardError> {
293:     let mut count = 0;
294:     let mut slice_vec = load_slices(circ);
295: 
296:     for slice_index in 0..slice_vec.len() {
297:         let slice_commands: Vec<_> = slice_vec[slice_index]
298:             .iter()
299:             .flatten()
300:             .unique()
301:             .cloned()
302:             .collect();
303: 
304:         for command in slice_commands {
305:             let Some((destination, new_nexts)) =
306:                 available_slice(&circ, &slice_vec, slice_index, &command)
307:             else {
308:                 continue;
309:             };
310: 
311:             debug_assert!(
312:                 destination < slice_index,
313:                 "Avoid mutating slices we haven't got to yet."
314:             );
315:             for q in command.qubits() {
316:                 let com = slice_vec[slice_index][q.index()].take();
317:                 slice_vec[destination][q.index()] = com;
318:             }
319:             let rewrite = PullForward { command, new_nexts };
320:             circ.apply_rewrite(rewrite)?;
321:             count += 1;
322:         }
323:     }
324:     Ok(count)
325: }

234: /// An iterator over the commands of a circuit.
235: #[derive(Clone)]
236: pub struct CommandIterator<'circ, Circ> {
237:     /// The circuit.
238:     circ: &'circ Circ,
239:     /// Toposorted nodes.
240:     nodes: NodeWalker,
241:     /// Last wire for each [`LinearUnit`] in the circuit.
242:     wire_unit: HashMap<Wire, usize>,
243:     /// Remaining commands, not counting I/O nodes.
244:     remaining: usize,
245:     /// Delayed output of constant and load const nodes. Contains nodes that
246:     /// haven't been yielded yet.
247:     ///
248:     /// We only yield them as Commands when their consumers require them.
249:     delayed_consts: HashSet<Node>,
250:     /// Nodes with delayed predecessors.
251:     ///
252:     /// Each node is associated with the number of predecessors that are present
253:     /// in `delayed_consts`.
254:     ///
255:     /// This map is used for performance, to avoid checking the neighbours vs
256:     /// the `delayed_consts` set for each processed node.
257:     delayed_consumers: HashMap<Node, usize>,
258:     /// The next node to be processed.
259:     ///
260:     /// This node was produced by the last call to `nodes.next()`, but we had to
261:     /// yield some delayed const nodes before it.
262:     delayed_node: Option<Node>,
263: }
264: 
265: impl<'circ, Circ> CommandIterator<'circ, Circ>
266: where
267:     Circ: Circuit,
268: {
269:     /// Create a new iterator over the commands of a circuit.
270:     pub(super) fn new(circ: &'circ Circ) -> Self {
271:         // Initialize the map assigning linear units to the input's linear
272:         // ports.
273:         //
274:         // TODO: `with_wires` combinator for `Units`?
275:         let wire_unit = circ
276:             .linear_units()
277:             .map(|(linear_unit, port, _)| {
278:                 let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
279:                 (Wire::new(circ.input(), port), linear_unit.index())
280:             })
281:             .collect();
282: 
283:         let nodes = pv::Topo::new(&circ.as_petgraph());
284:         Self {
285:             circ,
286:             nodes,
287:             wire_unit,
288:             // Ignore the input and output nodes, and the root.
289:             remaining: circ.node_count() - 3,
290:             delayed_consts: HashSet::new(),
291:             delayed_consumers: HashMap::new(),
292:             delayed_node: None,
293:         }
294:     }
295: 
296:     /// Returns the next node to be processed.
297:     ///
298:     /// If the next node in the topological order is a constant or load const node,
299:     /// delay it until its consumers are processed.
300:     fn next_node(&mut self) -> Option<Node> {
301:         let node = self
302:             .delayed_node
303:             .take()
304:             .or_else(|| self.nodes.next(&self.circ.as_petgraph()))?;
305: 
306:         // If this node is a constant or load const node, delay it.
307:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
308:         if tag == OpTag::Const || tag == OpTag::LoadConst {
309:             self.delayed_consts.insert(node);
310:             for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(node) {
311:                 *self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer).or_default() += 1;
312:             }
313:             return self.next_node();
314:         }
315: 
316:         // Check if we have any delayed const nodes that are consumed by this node.
317:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&node) {
318:             true => {
319:                 let delayed = self.next_delayed_node(node);
320:                 self.delayed_consts.remove(&delayed);
321:                 for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(delayed) {
322:                     let Entry::Occupied(mut entry) = self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer) else {
323:                         panic!("Delayed node consumer was not in delayed_consumers. Delayed node: {delayed:?}, consumer: {consumer:?}.");
324:                     };
325:                     *entry.get_mut() -= 1;
326:                     if *entry.get() == 0 {
327:                         entry.remove();
328:                     }
329:                 }
330:                 self.delayed_node = Some(node);
331:                 Some(delayed)
332:             }
333:             false => Some(node),
334:         }
335:     }
336: 
337:     /// Given a node with delayed predecessors, returns one of those predecessors.
338:     fn next_delayed_node(&mut self, consumer: Node) -> Node {
339:         let Some(delayed_pred) = self
340:             .circ
341:             .input_neighbours(consumer)
342:             .find(|k| self.delayed_consts.contains(k))
343:         else {
344:             panic!("Could not find a delayed predecessor for node {consumer:?}.");
345:         };
346: 
347:         // Only output this node if it doesn't require any other delayed predecessors.
348:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&delayed_pred) {
349:             true => self.next_delayed_node(delayed_pred),
350:             false => delayed_pred,
351:         }
352:     }
353: 
354:     /// Process a new node, updating wires in `unit_wires`.
355:     ///
356:     /// Returns the an option with the `linear_units` used to construct a
357:     /// [`Command`], if the node is not an input or output.
358:     ///
359:     /// We don't return the command directly to avoid lifetime issues due to the
360:     /// mutable borrow here.
361:     fn process_node(&mut self, node: Node) -> Option<Vec<LinearUnit>> {
362:         // The root node is ignored.
363:         if node == self.circ.root() {
364:             return None;
365:         }
366:         // Inputs and outputs are also ignored.
367:         // The input wire ids are already set in the `wire_unit` map during initialization.
368:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
369:         if tag == OpTag::Input || tag == OpTag::Output {
370:             return None;
371:         }
372: 
373:         // Collect the linear units passing through this command into the map
374:         // required to construct a `Command`.
375:         //
376:         // Updates the map tracking the last wire of linear units.
377:         let linear_units: Vec<_> =
378:             Units::new(self.circ, node, Direction::Outgoing, DefaultUnitLabeller)
379:                 .filter_units::<filter::Linear>()
380:                 .map(|(_, port, _)| {
381:                     // Find the linear unit id for this port.
382:                     let linear_id = self
383:                         .follow_linear_port(node, port)
384:                         .and_then(|input_port| {
385:                             let input_port = input_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
386:                             self.circ.linked_outputs(node, input_port).next()
387:                         })
388:                         .and_then(|(from, from_port)| {
389:                             // Remove the old wire from the map (if there was one)
390:                             self.wire_unit.remove(&Wire::new(from, from_port))
391:                         })
392:                         .unwrap_or({
393:                             // New linear unit found. Assign it a new id.
394:                             self.wire_unit.len()
395:                         });
396:                     // Update the map tracking the linear units
397:                     let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
398:                     let new_wire = Wire::new(node, port);
399:                     self.wire_unit.insert(new_wire, linear_id);
400:                     LinearUnit::new(linear_id)
401:                 })
402:                 .collect();
403: 
404:         Some(linear_units)
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Returns the linear port on the node that corresponds to the same linear unit.
408:     ///
409:     /// We assume the linear data uses the same port offsets on both sides of the node.
410:     /// In the future we may want to have a more general mechanism to handle this.
411:     //
412:     // Note that `Command::linear_units` assumes this behaviour.
413:     fn follow_linear_port(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Port> {
414:         let optype = self.circ.get_optype(node);
415:         if !optype.port_kind(port)?.is_linear() {
416:             return None;
417:         }
418:         let other_port = Port::new(port.direction().reverse(), port.index());
419:         if optype.port_kind(other_port) == optype.port_kind(port) {
420:             Some(other_port)
421:         } else {
422:             None
423:         }
424:     }
425: }

3: //! A [`CircuitUnit`] can either be a unique identifier for a linear unit (a
4: //! [`LinearUnit`]), or a wire between two HUGR nodes (a [`Wire`]).
5: //!
6: //! Linear units are tracked along the circuit, so values like qubits that are
7: //! used as input to a gate can continue to be tracked after the gate is
8: //! applied.
9: //!
10: //! The [`Units`] iterator defined in this module yields all the input or output
11: //! units of a node. See [`Circuit::units`] and [`Command`] for more details.
12: //!
13: //! [`Command`]: super::command::Command
14: 
15: pub mod filter;
16: pub use filter::FilteredUnits;
17: 
18: use std::iter::FusedIterator;
19: 
20: use hugr::types::{EdgeKind, Type, TypeRow};
21: use hugr::CircuitUnit;
22: use hugr::{Direction, Node, Port, Wire};
23: 
24: use crate::utils::type_is_linear;
25: 
26: use self::filter::UnitFilter;
27: 
28: use super::Circuit;
29: 
30: /// A linear unit id, used in [`CircuitUnit::Linear`].
31: // TODO: Add this to hugr?
32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
33: pub struct LinearUnit(usize);
34: 
35: impl LinearUnit {
36:     /// Creates a new [`LinearUnit`].
37:     pub fn new(index: usize) -> Self {
38:         Self(index)
39:     }
40:     /// Returns the index of this [`LinearUnit`].
41:     pub fn index(&self) -> usize {
42:         self.0
43:     }
44: }
45: 
46: impl From<LinearUnit> for CircuitUnit {
47:     fn from(lu: LinearUnit) -> Self {
48:         CircuitUnit::Linear(lu.index())
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: impl TryFrom<CircuitUnit> for LinearUnit {
53:     type Error = ();
54: 
55:     fn try_from(cu: CircuitUnit) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
56:         match cu {
57:             CircuitUnit::Wire(_) => Err(()),
58:             CircuitUnit::Linear(i) => Ok(LinearUnit(i)),
59:         }
60:     }
61: }
62: /// An iterator over the units in the input or output boundary of a [Node].
63: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
64: pub struct Units<UL = DefaultUnitLabeller> {
65:     /// The node of the circuit.
66:     node: Node,
67:     /// The direction of the boundary.
68:     direction: Direction,
69:     /// The types of the boundary.
70:     types: TypeRow,
71:     /// The current index in the type row.
72:     pos: usize,
73:     /// The number of linear units yielded so far.
74:     linear_count: usize,
75:     /// A pre-set assignment of units that maps linear ports to
76:     /// [`CircuitUnit::Linear`] ids.
77:     ///
78:     /// The default type is `()`, which assigns new linear ids sequentially.
79:     unit_labeller: UL,
80: }
81: 
82: impl Units<DefaultUnitLabeller> {
83:     /// Create a new iterator over the input units of a circuit.
84:     ///
85:     /// This iterator will yield all units originating from the circuit's input
86:     /// node.
87:     #[inline]
88:     pub(super) fn new_circ_input(circuit: &impl Circuit) -> Self {
89:         Self::new(
90:             circuit,
91:             circuit.input(),
92:             Direction::Outgoing,
93:             DefaultUnitLabeller,
94:         )
95:     }
96: }
97: 
98: impl<UL> Units<UL>
99: where
100:     UL: UnitLabeller,
101: {
102:     /// Apply a [`UnitFilter`] to the iterator's output, possibly unwrapping the
103:     /// [`CircuitUnit`] into either a linear unit or a wire.
104:     pub fn filter_units<F: UnitFilter>(self) -> FilteredUnits<F, UL> {
105:         self.filter_map(F::accept)
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Create a new iterator over the units of a node.
109:     //
110:     // Note that this ignores any incoming linear unit labels, and just assigns
111:     // new unit ids sequentially.
112:     #[inline]
113:     pub(super) fn new(
114:         circuit: &impl Circuit,
115:         node: Node,
116:         direction: Direction,
117:         unit_labeller: UL,
118:     ) -> Self {
119:         Self {
120:             node,
121:             direction,
122:             types: Self::init_types(circuit, node, direction),
123:             pos: 0,
124:             linear_count: 0,
125:             unit_labeller,
126:         }
127:     }
128: 
129:     /// Initialize the boundary types.
130:     ///
131:     /// We use a [`TypeRow`] to avoid allocating for simple boundaries, but if
132:     /// any static port is present we create a new owned [`TypeRow`] with them included.
133:     //
134:     // TODO: This is quite hacky, but we need it to accept Const static inputs.
135:     // We should revisit it once this is reworked on the HUGR side.
136:     fn init_types(circuit: &impl Circuit, node: Node, direction: Direction) -> TypeRow {
137:         let optype = circuit.get_optype(node);
138:         let sig = circuit.signature(node).unwrap_or_default();
139:         let mut types = match direction {
140:             Direction::Outgoing => sig.output,
141:             Direction::Incoming => sig.input,
142:         };
143:         if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(static_type)) = optype.static_port_kind(direction) {
144:             types.to_mut().push(static_type);
145:         };
146:         if let Some(EdgeKind::Static(other)) = optype.other_port_kind(direction) {
147:             types.to_mut().push(other);
148:         }
149:         types
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// Construct an output value to yield.
153:     ///
154:     /// Calls [`UnitLabeller::assign_linear`] to assign a linear unit id to the linear ports.
155:     /// Non-linear ports are assigned [`CircuitUnit::Wire`]s via [`UnitLabeller::assign_wire`].
156:     #[inline]
157:     fn make_value(&self, typ: &Type, port: Port) -> Option<(CircuitUnit, Port, Type)> {
158:         let unit = if type_is_linear(typ) {
159:             let linear_unit =
160:                 self.unit_labeller
161:                     .assign_linear(self.node, port, self.linear_count - 1);
162:             CircuitUnit::Linear(linear_unit.index())
163:         } else {
164:             let wire = self.unit_labeller.assign_wire(self.node, port)?;
165:             CircuitUnit::Wire(wire)
166:         };
167:         Some((unit, port, typ.clone()))
168:     }
169: }
170: 
171: impl<UL> Iterator for Units<UL>
172: where
173:     UL: UnitLabeller,
174: {
175:     type Item = (CircuitUnit, Port, Type);
176: 
177:     #[inline]
178:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
179:         loop {
180:             let typ = self.types.get(self.pos)?;
181:             let port = Port::new(self.direction, self.pos);
182:             self.pos += 1;
183:             if type_is_linear(typ) {
184:                 self.linear_count += 1;
185:             }
186:             if let Some(val) = self.make_value(typ, port) {
187:                 return Some(val);
188:             }
189:         }
190:     }
191: 
192:     fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
193:         let len = self.types.len() - self.pos;
194:         if self.direction == Direction::Outgoing {
195:             (len, Some(len))
196:         } else {
197:             // Even when yielding every unit, a disconnected input non-linear
198:             // port cannot be assigned a `CircuitUnit::Wire` and so it will be
199:             // skipped.
200:             (0, Some(len))
201:         }
202:     }
203: }
204: 
205: impl<UL> FusedIterator for Units<UL> where UL: UnitLabeller {}
206: 
207: /// A trait for assigning linear unit ids and wires to ports of a node.
208: pub trait UnitLabeller {
209:     /// Assign a linear unit id to an port.
210:     ///
211:     /// # Parameters
212:     /// - node: The node in the circuit.
213:     /// - port: The node's port in the node.
214:     /// - linear_count: The number of linear units yielded so far.
215:     fn assign_linear(&self, node: Node, port: Port, linear_count: usize) -> LinearUnit;
216: 
217:     /// Assign a wire to a port, if possible.
218:     ///
219:     /// # Parameters
220:     /// - node: The node in the circuit.
221:     /// - port: The node's port in the node.
222:     fn assign_wire(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Wire>;
223: }
224: 
225: /// The default [`UnitLabeller`] that assigns new linear unit ids
226: /// sequentially, and only assigns wires to an outgoing ports (as input ports
227: /// require querying the HUGR for their neighbours).
228: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
229: pub struct DefaultUnitLabeller;
230: 
231: impl UnitLabeller for DefaultUnitLabeller {
232:     #[inline]
233:     fn assign_linear(&self, _: Node, _: Port, linear_count: usize) -> LinearUnit {
234:         LinearUnit(linear_count)
235:     }
236: 
237:     #[inline]
238:     fn assign_wire(&self, node: Node, port: Port) -> Option<Wire> {
239:         let port = port.as_outgoing().ok()?;
240:         Some(Wire::new(node, port))
241:     }
242: }

234: /// An iterator over the commands of a circuit.

236: pub struct CommandIterator<'circ, Circ> {
237:     /// The circuit.
238:     circ: &'circ Circ,
239:     /// Toposorted nodes.
240:     nodes: NodeWalker,
241:     /// Last wire for each [`LinearUnit`] in the circuit.
242:     wire_unit: HashMap<Wire, usize>,
243:     /// Remaining commands, not counting I/O nodes.
244:     remaining: usize,

247:     ///
248:     /// We only yield them as Commands when their consumers require them.
249:     delayed_consts: HashSet<Node>,
250:     /// Nodes with delayed predecessors.
251:     ///
252:     /// Each node is associated with the number of predecessors that are present
253:     /// in `delayed_consts`.
254:     ///
255:     /// This map is used for performance, to avoid checking the neighbours vs
256:     /// the `delayed_consts` set for each processed node.
257:     delayed_consumers: HashMap<Node, usize>,
258:     /// The next node to be processed.

265: impl<'circ, Circ> CommandIterator<'circ, Circ>
266: where
267:     Circ: Circuit,
268: {
269:     /// Create a new iterator over the commands of a circuit.
270:     pub(super) fn new(circ: &'circ Circ) -> Self {

272:         // ports.
273:         //
274:         // TODO: `with_wires` combinator for `Units`?
275:         let wire_unit = circ
276:             .linear_units()
277:             .map(|(linear_unit, port, _)| {
278:                 let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
279:                 (Wire::new(circ.input(), port), linear_unit.index())
280:             })
281:             .collect();
282: 
283:         let nodes = pv::Topo::new(&circ.as_petgraph());
284:         Self {
285:             circ,
286:             nodes,
287:             wire_unit,
288:             // Ignore the input and output nodes, and the root.
289:             remaining: circ.node_count() - 3,
290:             delayed_consts: HashSet::new(),
291:             delayed_consumers: HashMap::new(),
292:             delayed_node: None,
293:         }
294:     }

296:     /// Returns the next node to be processed.
297:     ///
298:     /// If the next node in the topological order is a constant or load const node,
299:     /// delay it until its consumers are processed.
300:     fn next_node(&mut self) -> Option<Node> {
301:         let node = self
302:             .delayed_node
303:             .take()
304:             .or_else(|| self.nodes.next(&self.circ.as_petgraph()))?;
305: 
306:         // If this node is a constant or load const node, delay it.
307:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();
308:         if tag == OpTag::Const || tag == OpTag::LoadConst {
309:             self.delayed_consts.insert(node);
310:             for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(node) {
311:                 *self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer).or_default() += 1;
312:             }
313:             return self.next_node();
314:         }
315: 
316:         // Check if we have any delayed const nodes that are consumed by this node.
317:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&node) {
318:             true => {
319:                 let delayed = self.next_delayed_node(node);
320:                 self.delayed_consts.remove(&delayed);
321:                 for consumer in self.circ.output_neighbours(delayed) {
322:                     let Entry::Occupied(mut entry) = self.delayed_consumers.entry(consumer) else {
323:                         panic!("Delayed node consumer was not in delayed_consumers. Delayed node: {delayed:?}, consumer: {consumer:?}.");
324:                     };
325:                     *entry.get_mut() -= 1;
326:                     if *entry.get() == 0 {
327:                         entry.remove();
328:                     }
329:                 }
330:                 self.delayed_node = Some(node);
331:                 Some(delayed)
332:             }
333:             false => Some(node),
334:         }
335:     }

337:     /// Given a node with delayed predecessors, returns one of those predecessors.
338:     fn next_delayed_node(&mut self, consumer: Node) -> Node {
339:         let Some(delayed_pred) = self
340:             .circ
341:             .input_neighbours(consumer)
342:             .find(|k| self.delayed_consts.contains(k))
343:         else {
344:             panic!("Could not find a delayed predecessor for node {consumer:?}.");
345:         };
346: 
347:         // Only output this node if it doesn't require any other delayed predecessors.
348:         match self.delayed_consumers.contains_key(&delayed_pred) {
349:             true => self.next_delayed_node(delayed_pred),
350:             false => delayed_pred,
351:         }
352:     }

354:     /// Process a new node, updating wires in `unit_wires`.
355:     ///
356:     /// Returns the an option with the `linear_units` used to construct a
357:     /// [`Command`], if the node is not an input or output.
358:     ///

360:     /// mutable borrow here.
361:     fn process_node(&mut self, node: Node) -> Option<Vec<LinearUnit>> {
362:         // The root node is ignored.
363:         if node == self.circ.root() {
364:             return None;
365:         }
366:         // Inputs and outputs are also ignored.
367:         // The input wire ids are already set in the `wire_unit` map during initialization.
368:         let tag = self.circ.get_optype(node).tag();

370:             return None;
371:         }

373:         // Collect the linear units passing through this command into the map
374:         // required to construct a `Command`.

376:         // Updates the map tracking the last wire of linear units.
377:         let linear_units: Vec<_> =

380:                 .map(|(_, port, _)| {
381:                     // Find the linear unit id for this port.
382:                     let linear_id = self
383:                         .follow_linear_port(node, port)
384:                         .and_then(|input_port| {
385:                             let input_port = input_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
386:                             self.circ.linked_outputs(node, input_port).next()
387:                         })
388:                         .and_then(|(from, from_port)| {
389:                             // Remove the old wire from the map (if there was one)
390:                             self.wire_unit.remove(&Wire::new(from, from_port))

392:                         .unwrap_or({

394:                             self.wire_unit.len()

397:                     let port = port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
398:                     let new_wire = Wire::new(node, port);

13: /// The cost for a group of operations in a circuit, each with cost `OpCost`.
14: pub trait CircuitCost: Add<Output = Self> + Sum<Self> + Debug + Default + Clone + Ord {
15:     /// The cost delta between two costs.
16:     type CostDelta: CostDelta;
17: 
18:     /// Return the cost as a `usize`. This may discard some of the cost information.
19:     fn as_usize(&self) -> usize;
20: 
21:     /// Return the cost delta between two costs.
22:     fn sub_cost(&self, other: &Self) -> Self::CostDelta;
23: 
24:     /// Adds a cost delta to the cost.
25:     fn add_delta(&self, delta: &Self::CostDelta) -> Self;
26: 
27:     /// Divide the cost, rounded up.
28:     fn div_cost(&self, n: NonZeroUsize) -> Self;
29: }

32: pub trait CostDelta:
33:     AddAssign + Add<Output = Self> + Sum<Self> + Debug + Default + Clone + Ord

39: /// A pair of major and minor cost.
40: ///
41: /// This is used to order circuits based on major cost first, then minor cost.
42: /// A typical example would be CX count as major cost and total gate count as
43: /// minor cost.
44: pub type MajorMinorCost<T = usize> = LexicographicCost<T, 2>;

46: impl<const N: usize, V, T> From<V> for LexicographicCost<T, N>
47: where
48:     V: Into<[T; N]>,

52:     }

55: /// A cost that is ordered lexicographically.
56: ///
57: /// An array of cost functions, where the first one is infinitely more important
58: /// than the second, which is infinitely more important than the third, etc.
59: #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
60: pub struct LexicographicCost<T, const N: usize>([T; N]);
61: 
62: impl<const N: usize, T: Default + Copy> Default for LexicographicCost<T, N> {
63:     fn default() -> Self {
64:         Self([Default::default(); N])
65:     }
66: }

68: // Serialise as string so that it is easy to write to CSV

70:     fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
71:     where
72:         S: serde::Serializer,
73:     {
74:         serializer.serialize_str(&format!("{:?}", self))

85: impl<T: Add<Output = T> + Copy, const N: usize> Add for LexicographicCost<T, N> {
86:     type Output = Self;
87: 
88:     fn add(mut self, rhs: Self) -> Self::Output {
89:         for i in 0..N {
90:             self.0[i] = self.0[i] + rhs.0[i];
91:         }
92:         self
93:     }
94: }

96: impl<T: AddAssign + Copy, const N: usize> AddAssign for LexicographicCost<T, N> {
97:     fn add_assign(&mut self, rhs: Self) {
98:         for i in 0..N {
99:             self.0[i] += rhs.0[i];
100:         }
101:     }
102: }

104: impl<T: Add<Output = T> + Default + Copy, const N: usize> Sum for LexicographicCost<T, N> {
105:     fn sum<I: Iterator<Item = Self>>(iter: I) -> Self {
106:         iter.reduce(|a, b| a + b).unwrap_or_default()
107:     }
108: }

111:     #[inline]
112:     fn as_isize(&self) -> isize {
113:         if N > 0 {
114:             self.0[0]
115:         } else {
116:             0
117:         }
118:     }

121: impl<const N: usize> CircuitCost for LexicographicCost<usize, N> {
122:     type CostDelta = LexicographicCost<isize, N>;
123: 
124:     #[inline]
125:     fn as_usize(&self) -> usize {
126:         if N > 0 {
127:             self.0[0]
128:         } else {
129:             0
130:         }
131:     }
132: 
133:     #[inline]
134:     fn sub_cost(&self, other: &Self) -> Self::CostDelta {
135:         let mut costdelta = [0; N];
136:         for (delta, &a, &b) in izip!(costdelta.iter_mut(), &self.0, &other.0) {
137:             *delta = (a as isize) - (b as isize);
138:         }
139:         LexicographicCost(costdelta)
140:     }
141: 
142:     #[inline]
143:     fn add_delta(&self, delta: &Self::CostDelta) -> Self {
144:         let mut ret = [0; N];
145:         for (add, &a, &b) in izip!(ret.iter_mut(), &self.0, &delta.0) {
146:             *add = a.saturating_add_signed(b);
147:         }
148:         Self(ret)
149:     }
150: 
151:     #[inline]
152:     fn div_cost(&self, n: NonZeroUsize) -> Self {
153:         let mut ret = [0; N];
154:         for (div, &a) in ret.iter_mut().zip(&self.0) {
155:             *div = (a.saturating_sub(1)) / n.get() + 1;
156:         }
157:         Self(ret)
158:     }
159: }

162:     #[inline]
163:     fn as_isize(&self) -> isize {
164:         *self
165:     }
166: }

168: impl CircuitCost for usize {
169:     type CostDelta = isize;

172:     fn as_usize(&self) -> usize {
173:         *self
174:     }
175: 
176:     #[inline]
177:     fn sub_cost(&self, other: &Self) -> Self::CostDelta {
178:         (*self as isize) - (*other as isize)
179:     }
180: 
181:     #[inline]
182:     fn add_delta(&self, delta: &Self::CostDelta) -> Self {
183:         self.saturating_add_signed(*delta)
184:     }
185: 
186:     #[inline]
187:     fn div_cost(&self, n: NonZeroUsize) -> Self {
188:         (self.saturating_sub(1)) / n.get() + 1
189:     }

1: //! This module provides a utility to split a circuit into chunks, and reassemble them afterwards.
2: //!
3: //! See [`CircuitChunks`] for more information.
4: 
5: use std::collections::HashMap;
6: use std::mem;
7: use std::ops::{Index, IndexMut};
8: 
9: use derive_more::From;
10: use hugr::builder::{Container, FunctionBuilder};
11: use hugr::hugr::hugrmut::HugrMut;
12: use hugr::hugr::views::sibling_subgraph::TopoConvexChecker;
13: use hugr::hugr::views::{HierarchyView, SiblingGraph, SiblingSubgraph};
14: use hugr::hugr::{HugrError, NodeMetadataMap};
15: use hugr::ops::handle::DataflowParentID;
16: use hugr::ops::OpType;
17: use hugr::types::FunctionType;
18: use hugr::{Hugr, HugrView, IncomingPort, Node, OutgoingPort, PortIndex, Wire};
19: use itertools::Itertools;
20: use portgraph::algorithms::ConvexChecker;
21: 
22: use crate::Circuit;

26: /// An identifier for the connection between chunks.
27: ///
28: /// This is based on the wires of the original circuit.
29: ///
30: /// When reassembling the circuit, the input/output wires of each chunk are
31: /// re-linked by matching these identifiers.
32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, From)]
33: pub struct ChunkConnection(Wire);
34: 
35: /// A chunk of a circuit.
36: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
37: pub struct Chunk {
38:     /// The extracted circuit.
39:     pub circ: Hugr,
40:     /// The original wires connected to the input.
41:     inputs: Vec<ChunkConnection>,
42:     /// The original wires connected to the output.
43:     outputs: Vec<ChunkConnection>,
44: }
45: 
46: impl Chunk {
47:     /// Extract a chunk from a circuit.
48:     ///
49:     /// The chunk is extracted from the input wires to the output wires.
50:     pub(self) fn extract<H: HugrView>(
51:         circ: &H,
52:         nodes: impl IntoIterator<Item = Node>,
53:         checker: &impl ConvexChecker,
54:     ) -> Self {
55:         let subgraph = SiblingSubgraph::try_from_nodes_with_checker(
56:             nodes.into_iter().collect_vec(),
57:             circ,
58:             checker,
59:         )
60:         .expect("Failed to define the chunk subgraph");
61:         let extracted = subgraph
62:             .extract_subgraph(circ, "Chunk")
63:             .expect("Failed to extract chunk");
64:         // Transform the subgraph's input/output sets into wires that can be
65:         // matched between different chunks.
66:         //
67:         // This requires finding the `Outgoing` port corresponding to each
68:         // subgraph input.
69:         let inputs = subgraph
70:             .incoming_ports()
71:             .iter()
72:             .map(|wires| {
73:                 let (inp_node, inp_port) = wires[0];
74:                 let (out_node, out_port) = circ
75:                     .linked_outputs(inp_node, inp_port)
76:                     .exactly_one()
77:                     .ok()
78:                     .unwrap();
79:                 Wire::new(out_node, out_port).into()
80:             })
81:             .collect();
82:         let outputs = subgraph
83:             .outgoing_ports()
84:             .iter()
85:             .map(|&(node, port)| Wire::new(node, port).into())
86:             .collect();
87:         Self {
88:             circ: extracted,
89:             inputs,
90:             outputs,
91:         }
92:     }
93: 
94:     /// Insert the chunk back into a circuit.
95:     pub(self) fn insert(&self, circ: &mut impl HugrMut, root: Node) -> ChunkInsertResult {
96:         if self.circ.children(self.circ.root()).nth(2).is_none() {
97:             // The chunk is empty. We don't need to insert anything.
98:             return self.empty_chunk_insert_result();
99:         }
100: 
101:         let [chunk_inp, chunk_out] = self.circ.get_io(self.circ.root()).unwrap();
102:         let chunk_sg: SiblingGraph<'_, DataflowParentID> =
103:             SiblingGraph::try_new(&self.circ, self.circ.root()).unwrap();
104:         // Insert the chunk circuit into the original circuit.
105:         let subgraph = SiblingSubgraph::try_new_dataflow_subgraph(&chunk_sg)
106:             .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("The chunk circuit is no longer a dataflow graph: {e}"));
107:         let node_map = circ
108:             .insert_subgraph(root, &self.circ, &subgraph)
109:             .expect("Failed to insert the chunk subgraph");
110: 
111:         let mut input_map = HashMap::with_capacity(self.inputs.len());
112:         let mut output_map = HashMap::with_capacity(self.outputs.len());
113: 
114:         // Translate each connection from the chunk input into a [`ConnectionTarget`].
115:         //
116:         // Connections to an inserted node are translated into a [`ConnectionTarget::InsertedNode`].
117:         // Connections from the input directly into the output become a [`ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection`].
118:         for (&connection, chunk_inp_port) in
119:             self.inputs.iter().zip(self.circ.node_outputs(chunk_inp))
120:         {
121:             let connection_targets: Vec<ConnectionTarget> = self
122:                 .circ
123:                 .linked_inputs(chunk_inp, chunk_inp_port)
124:                 .map(|(node, port)| {
125:                     if node == chunk_out {
126:                         // This was a direct wire from the chunk input to the output. Use the output's [`ChunkConnection`].
127:                         let output_connection = self.outputs[port.index()];
128:                         ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(output_connection)
129:                     } else {
130:                         // Translate the original chunk node into the inserted node.
131:                         ConnectionTarget::InsertedInput(*node_map.get(&node).unwrap(), port)
132:                     }
133:                 })
134:                 .collect();
135:             input_map.insert(connection, connection_targets);
136:         }
137: 
138:         for (&wire, chunk_out_port) in self.outputs.iter().zip(self.circ.node_inputs(chunk_out)) {
139:             let (node, port) = self
140:                 .circ
141:                 .linked_outputs(chunk_out, chunk_out_port)
142:                 .exactly_one()
143:                 .ok()
144:                 .unwrap();
145:             let target = if node == chunk_inp {
146:                 // This was a direct wire from the chunk output to the input. Use the input's [`ChunkConnection`].
147:                 let input_connection = self.inputs[port.index()];
148:                 ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(input_connection)
149:             } else {
150:                 // Translate the original chunk node into the inserted node.
151:                 ConnectionTarget::InsertedOutput(*node_map.get(&node).unwrap(), port)
152:             };
153:             output_map.insert(wire, target);
154:         }
155: 
156:         ChunkInsertResult {
157:             incoming_connections: input_map,
158:             outgoing_connections: output_map,
159:         }
160:     }
161: 
162:     /// Compute the return value for `insert` when the chunk is empty (Subgraph would throw an error in this case).
163:     ///
164:     /// TODO: Support empty Subgraphs in Hugr?
165:     fn empty_chunk_insert_result(&self) -> ChunkInsertResult {
166:         let [chunk_inp, chunk_out] = self.circ.get_io(self.circ.root()).unwrap();
167:         let mut input_map = HashMap::with_capacity(self.inputs.len());
168:         let mut output_map = HashMap::with_capacity(self.outputs.len());
169: 
170:         for (&connection, chunk_inp_port) in
171:             self.inputs.iter().zip(self.circ.node_outputs(chunk_inp))
172:         {
173:             let connection_targets: Vec<ConnectionTarget> = self
174:                 .circ
175:                 .linked_ports(chunk_inp, chunk_inp_port)
176:                 .map(|(node, port)| {
177:                     assert_eq!(node, chunk_out);
178:                     let output_connection = self.outputs[port.index()];
179:                     ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(output_connection)
180:                 })
181:                 .collect();
182:             input_map.insert(connection, connection_targets);
183:         }
184: 
185:         for (&wire, chunk_out_port) in self.outputs.iter().zip(self.circ.node_inputs(chunk_out)) {
186:             let (node, port) = self
187:                 .circ
188:                 .linked_ports(chunk_out, chunk_out_port)
189:                 .exactly_one()
190:                 .ok()
191:                 .unwrap();
192:             assert_eq!(node, chunk_inp);
193:             let input_connection = self.inputs[port.index()];
194:             output_map.insert(
195:                 wire,
196:                 ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(input_connection),
197:             );
198:         }
199: 
200:         ChunkInsertResult {
201:             incoming_connections: input_map,
202:             outgoing_connections: output_map,
203:         }
204:     }

255:     /// Split a circuit into chunks.
256:     ///
257:     /// The circuit is split into chunks of at most `max_size` gates.
258:     pub fn split(circ: &impl Circuit, max_size: usize) -> Self {
259:         Self::split_with_cost(circ, max_size.saturating_sub(1), |_| 1)
260:     }
261: 
262:     /// Split a circuit into chunks.
263:     ///
264:     /// The circuit is split into chunks of at most `max_cost`, using the provided cost function.
265:     pub fn split_with_cost<H: Circuit, C: CircuitCost>(
266:         circ: &H,
267:         max_cost: C,
268:         op_cost: impl Fn(&OpType) -> C,
269:     ) -> Self {
270:         let root_meta = circ.get_node_metadata(circ.root()).cloned();
271:         let signature = circ.circuit_signature().clone();
272: 
273:         let [circ_input, circ_output] = circ.get_io(circ.root()).unwrap();
274:         let input_connections = circ
275:             .node_outputs(circ_input)
276:             .map(|port| Wire::new(circ_input, port).into())
277:             .collect();
278:         let output_connections = circ
279:             .node_inputs(circ_output)
280:             .flat_map(|p| circ.linked_outputs(circ_output, p))
281:             .map(|(n, p)| Wire::new(n, p).into())
282:             .collect();
283: 
284:         let mut chunks = Vec::new();
285:         let convex_checker = TopoConvexChecker::new(circ);
286:         let mut running_cost = C::default();
287:         let mut current_group = 0;
288:         for (_, commands) in &circ.commands().map(|cmd| cmd.node()).group_by(|&node| {
289:             let new_cost = running_cost.clone() + op_cost(circ.get_optype(node));
290:             if new_cost.sub_cost(&max_cost).as_isize() > 0 {
291:                 running_cost = C::default();
292:                 current_group += 1;
293:             } else {
294:                 running_cost = new_cost;
295:             }
296:             current_group
297:         }) {
298:             chunks.push(Chunk::extract(circ, commands, &convex_checker));
299:         }
300:         Self {
301:             signature,
302:             root_meta,
303:             input_connections,
304:             output_connections,
305:             chunks,
306:         }
307:     }

309:     /// Reassemble the chunks into a circuit.
310:     pub fn reassemble(self) -> Result<Hugr, HugrError> {
311:         let name = self
312:             .root_meta
313:             .as_ref()
314:             .and_then(|map| map.get("name"))
315:             .and_then(|s| s.as_str())
316:             .unwrap_or("");
317: 
318:         let mut builder = FunctionBuilder::new(name, self.signature.into()).unwrap();
319:         // Take the unfinished Hugr from the builder, to avoid unnecessary
320:         // validation checks that require connecting the inputs an outputs.
321:         let mut reassembled = mem::take(builder.hugr_mut());
322:         let root = reassembled.root();
323:         let [reassembled_input, reassembled_output] = reassembled.get_io(root).unwrap();
324: 
325:         // The chunks input and outputs are each identified with a
326:         // [`ChunkConnection`]. We collect both sides first, and rewire them
327:         // after the chunks have been inserted.
328:         let mut sources: HashMap<ChunkConnection, (Node, OutgoingPort)> = HashMap::new();
329:         let mut targets: HashMap<ChunkConnection, Vec<(Node, IncomingPort)>> = HashMap::new();
330: 
331:         // A map for `ChunkConnection`s that have been merged into another (due
332:         // to identity wires in the updated chunks).
333:         //
334:         // Maps each `ChunkConnection` to the `ChunkConnection` it has been
335:         // merged into.
336:         //
337:         // This is a poor man's Union Find. Since we traverse the chunks in
338:         // order, we can assume that already seen connections will not be merged
339:         // again.
340:         let mut transitive_connections: HashMap<ChunkConnection, ChunkConnection> = HashMap::new();
341:         let get_merged_connection = |transitive_connections: &HashMap<_, _>, connection| {
342:             transitive_connections
343:                 .get(&connection)
344:                 .copied()
345:                 .unwrap_or(connection)
346:         };
347: 
348:         // Register the source ports for the `ChunkConnections` in the circuit input.
349:         for (&connection, port) in self
350:             .input_connections
351:             .iter()
352:             .zip(reassembled.node_outputs(reassembled_input))
353:         {
354:             sources.insert(connection, (reassembled_input, port));
355:         }
356: 
357:         for chunk in self.chunks {
358:             // Insert the chunk circuit without its input/output nodes.
359:             let ChunkInsertResult {
360:                 incoming_connections,
361:                 outgoing_connections,
362:             } = chunk.insert(&mut reassembled, root);
363:             // Associate the chunk's inserted inputs and outputs to the
364:             // `ChunkConnection` identifiers, so we can re-connect everything
365:             // afterwards.
366:             //
367:             // The chunk may return `ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection`s to
368:             // indicate that a `ChunkConnection` has been merged into another
369:             // (due to an identity wire).
370:             for (connection, conn_target) in outgoing_connections {
371:                 match conn_target {
372:                     ConnectionTarget::InsertedOutput(node, port) => {
373:                         // The output of a chunk always has fresh `ChunkConnection`s.
374:                         sources.insert(connection, (node, port));
375:                     }
376:                     ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(merged_connection) => {
377:                         // The output's `ChunkConnection` has been merged into one of the input's.
378:                         let merged_connection =
379:                             get_merged_connection(&transitive_connections, merged_connection);
380:                         transitive_connections.insert(connection, merged_connection);
381:                     }
382:                     _ => panic!("Unexpected connection target"),
383:                 }
384:             }
385:             for (connection, conn_targets) in incoming_connections {
386:                 // The connection in the chunk's input may have been merged into a earlier one.
387:                 let connection = get_merged_connection(&transitive_connections, connection);
388:                 for tgt in conn_targets {
389:                     match tgt {
390:                         ConnectionTarget::InsertedInput(node, port) => {
391:                             targets.entry(connection).or_default().push((node, port));
392:                         }
393:                         ConnectionTarget::TransitiveConnection(_merged_connection) => {
394:                             // The merge has been registered when scanning the
395:                             // outgoing_connections, so we don't need to do
396:                             // anything here.
397:                         }
398:                         _ => panic!("Unexpected connection target"),
399:                     }
400:                 }
401:             }
402:         }
403: 
404:         // Register the target ports for the `ChunkConnections` into the circuit output.
405:         for (&connection, port) in self
406:             .output_connections
407:             .iter()
408:             .zip(reassembled.node_inputs(reassembled_output))
409:         {
410:             // The connection in the chunk's input may have been merged into a earlier one.
411:             let connection = get_merged_connection(&transitive_connections, connection);
412:             targets
413:                 .entry(connection)
414:                 .or_default()
415:                 .push((reassembled_output, port));
416:         }
417: 
418:         // Reconnect the different chunks.
419:         for (connection, (source, source_port)) in sources {
420:             let Some(tgts) = targets.remove(&connection) else {
421:                 continue;
422:             };
423:             for (target, target_port) in tgts {
424:                 reassembled.connect(source, source_port, target, target_port)?;
425:             }
426:         }
427: 
428:         reassembled.overwrite_node_metadata(root, self.root_meta)?;
429: 
430:         Ok(reassembled)
431:     }

159: /// Remove an empty wire in a dataflow HUGR.
160: ///
161: /// The wire to be removed is identified by the index of the outgoing port
162: /// at the circuit input node.
163: ///
164: /// This will change the circuit signature and will shift all ports after
165: /// the removed wire by -1. If the wire is connected to the output node,
166: /// this will also change the signature output and shift the ports after
167: /// the removed wire by -1.
168: ///
169: /// This will return an error if the wire is not empty or if a HugrError
170: /// occurs.
171: #[allow(dead_code)]
172: pub(crate) fn remove_empty_wire(
173:     circ: &mut impl HugrMut,
174:     input_port: usize,
175: ) -> Result<(), CircuitMutError> {
176:     let [inp, out] = circ.get_io(circ.root()).expect("no IO nodes found at root");
177:     if input_port >= circ.num_outputs(inp) {
178:         return Err(CircuitMutError::InvalidPortOffset(input_port));
179:     }
180:     let input_port = Port::new(Direction::Outgoing, input_port);
181:     let link = circ
182:         .linked_ports(inp, input_port)
183:         .at_most_one()
184:         .map_err(|_| CircuitMutError::DeleteNonEmptyWire(input_port.index()))?;
185:     if link.is_some() && link.unwrap().0 != out {
186:         return Err(CircuitMutError::DeleteNonEmptyWire(input_port.index()));
187:     }
188:     if link.is_some() {
189:         circ.disconnect(inp, input_port)?;
190:     }
191: 
192:     // Shift ports at input
193:     shift_ports(circ, inp, input_port, circ.num_outputs(inp))?;
194:     // Shift ports at output
195:     if let Some((out, output_port)) = link {
196:         shift_ports(circ, out, output_port, circ.num_inputs(out))?;
197:     }
198:     // Update input node, output node (if necessary) and root signatures.
199:     update_signature(circ, input_port.index(), link.map(|(_, p)| p.index()));
200:     // Resize ports at input/output node
201:     circ.set_num_ports(inp, 0, circ.num_outputs(inp) - 1);
202:     if let Some((out, _)) = link {
203:         circ.set_num_ports(out, circ.num_inputs(out) - 1, 0);
204:     }
205:     Ok(())

224: /// Shift ports in range (free_port + 1 .. max_ind) by -1.
225: fn shift_ports<C: HugrMut + ?Sized>(
226:     circ: &mut C,
227:     node: Node,
228:     mut free_port: Port,
229:     max_ind: usize,
230: ) -> Result<Port, hugr::hugr::HugrError> {
231:     let dir = free_port.direction();
232:     let port_range = (free_port.index() + 1..max_ind).map(|p| Port::new(dir, p));
233:     for port in port_range {
234:         let links = circ.linked_ports(node, port).collect_vec();
235:         if !links.is_empty() {
236:             circ.disconnect(node, port)?;
237:         }
238:         for (other_n, other_p) in links {
239:             match other_p.as_directed() {
240:                 Right(other_p) => {
241:                     let dst_port = free_port.as_incoming().unwrap();
242:                     circ.connect(other_n, other_p, node, dst_port)
243:                 }
244:                 Left(other_p) => {
245:                     let src_port = free_port.as_outgoing().unwrap();
246:                     circ.connect(node, src_port, other_n, other_p)
247:                 }
248:             }?;
249:         }
250:         free_port = port;
251:     }
252:     Ok(free_port)
253: }

266:             panic!("invalid circuit")

270:         types.into()

279:         let out = circ.output();
280:         let out_types: TypeRow = {
